body:
• Adjusted EBITDA £53.3m, up 34.6% YoY (margin 5.8% vs 3.3%), following two trading upgrades during the year; every brand now profitable at Adjusted EBITDA level.
  • Group GMV (pre returns) fell 21.6% to £1,820.7m as focus shifted to profitable sales; GMV improved sequentially each quarter through FY26.
  • Revenue down 24.7% to £917.0m — fall greater than GMV post-returns (-19.7%) due to marketplace mix shift (commission-only recognition).
  • Gross margin +40bps to 51.1% — first improvement since FY22, driven by marketplace sales recognised at 100% margin.
  • Debenhams brand: GMV +11.6% to £730m (now largest brand in Group); Adjusted EBITDA +38.5% to £34.8m (65.3% of Group EBITDA); marketplace scaled to 25,000+ partner brands (from c.15,000); 5.7m active customers; FY22-FY26 GMV CAGR 53.4%.
  • PrettyLittleThing turnaround: £15m swing to £14.0m Adjusted EBITDA profit (FY25: £1m loss); Board decided in January 2026 to retain PLT within continuing operations; FY25 restated on that basis.
  • Marketplace mix rose to 34.1% of GMV (FY25: 23.3%); marketplace GMV +14.9% to £620.4m.
  • Returns rate improved 160bps to 28.2%, aided by marketplace mix and product fit investment.
  • Operating costs -28.2% to £415.4m; fixed cost exit rate cut to £119m (vs £130m guided, FY25: £175m); on track for £100m exit rate in FY27 — c.£200m cumulative reduction by new management.
  • Adjusted EBIT returned to profit at £7.0m (FY25: £30.5m loss); Loss before tax narrowed 69.2% to £108.6m; statutory loss after tax down £218.1m to £108.3m; exceptionals fell to £68.1m (FY25: £271.7m).
  • Free cash flow improved to -£18.4m (FY25: -£40.2m); capex reduced to £16.0m (FY25: £27.5m).
  • Net debt £93.2m (1.75x Adjusted EBITDA) vs £78.2m; FY27 target <1x.
  • Refinanced in August 2025 to a new £175m facility maturing August 2028 (drawn £143.7m); completed oversubscribed £40m equity raise in February 2026 at 18p/share.
  • Headcount reduced to ~1,500 (from 6,189 in January 2024); warehouse consolidation into automated Sheffield DC delivering c.£33m recurring savings; single AI-powered tech platform saving c.£38m annually; 150+ contracts renegotiated for c.£35m savings.
  • Current trading: Q1 FY27 Group GMV +0.5% YoY, May 2026 ~+8%, June trading "continuing to be strong" — described as "a significant inflection point."
  • FY27 guidance: double-digit improvement in Adjusted EBITDA; net debt <1x EBITDA by year end; depreciation falling from £46.3m to ~£20m; capex ~£8m; lease payments ~£13m in FY27, ~£8m FY28, ~£6m FY29; exceptional costs expected to reduce materially; FY27 expected to deliver sustained free cash flow generation and a return to profit before tax.
  • US distribution centre sublease (Elizabethtown, PA) to ID Logistics agreed post period-end for remaining ~8.5 years: $9.5m (£7.1m) average annual rent income; ~$20m (£15m) of lease costs covered; triggers expected ~£40m non-cash exceptional credit in H1 FY27, strengthening net asset position.
  • Burnley warehouse classified as held for sale at £26.0m after £33.1m impairment; Units 1 & 3 sold post period-end for £5.0m in April 2026.
  • International expansion: Debenhams marketplace launched in US via Macy's, Bloomingdale's, Nordstrom and Amazon Fashion (~600m monthly shoppers); also live in Ireland and Australia.
  • Lost significant influence over Revolution Beauty on 19 Feb 2026; reclassified from associate to FVOCI investment (£8.5m carrying value); £3.5m fair value gain recognised, offset by £8.1m share of losses prior to reclassification.
  • No dividend recommended.
  • Inventory £105.3m (FY25: £72.2m underlying / £93.1m including held-for-sale) — net higher due to lower prior-year provisions; gross stock reduced in line with marketplace shift.
  • CEO Dan Finley: "This has been a year of significant and successful transformation for Debenhams Group...The turnaround is firmly on track...the best is yet to come."
  • Clear medium-term target: £1bn GMV and £50m+ EBITDA at Debenhams brand within three years.

body:
• Portfolio company Istesso has commenced dosing in IST-03, a Phase 2 randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of lead candidate leramistat in patients with sarcopenia caused by rheumatoid arthritis.
  • Trial evaluates effects on muscle quality, repair and function; sarcopenia currently has no specific pharmacological therapies available.
  • Builds on prior RA data showing leramistat improved disability/fatigue and reduced markers of muscle loss, plus preclinical data showing muscle recovery in aged animals to levels above younger baseline.
  • Leramistat is the lead asset from Istesso's novel Mitochondrial Complex I Modulators (MCMs) class, targeting adaptive tissue repair across muscle, bone, gut and lung.
  • Enrolment underway at Newcastle University and Newcastle Hospitals with NIHR support.
  • IP Group holds an undiluted 56.5% stake in Istesso.
  • CEO Greg Smith: "This marks an important inflection point for Istesso as it moves into Phase 2 evaluation of a genuinely novel approach to regenerative medicine. The programme is supported by a consistent body of clinical and preclinical data, and we believe the potential to influence underlying tissue repair represents a differentiated and scalable opportunity. Success here would be an important validation of the approach and open up multiple opportunities across large areas of unmet need."

  • CEO Dan Finley: "This is a significant development. The US DC was a major contributor to the challenges that the company has faced. One of my first actions in role was to close the US DC and the sublease of it mitigates a material future liability. Our turnaround strategy continues at pace."

• Voluntary public takeover offer for all HUGO BOSS AG shares not already owned by Frasers, made under the German Securities Acquisition and Takeover Act.
  • Cash offer price: €38.00 per HUGO BOSS share; aggregate consideration of ~€1,978.0m (~£1,727.1m) for the 73.94% of share capital / 73.42% of voting rights not held.
  • Frasers already holds 18,347,461 shares (26.06% of capital, 26.58% of voting rights) plus significant sold put options; move pre-empts mandatory offer trigger that would arise above 30%.
  • Net consideration on outstanding put options under Prior Trades could reach ~€1,143.3m (~£998.3m) for an interest in 34.3m shares (expiries up to December 2029).
  • No minimum acceptance threshold; conditional only on merger control clearances.
  • Expected completion H2 2026, subject to BaFin approval of the offer document and regulatory clearances.
  • Financing: new Acquisition Facility Agreement signed 10 June 2026 with BNP Paribas, Deutsche Bank Luxembourg, NatWest and Standard Chartered; unsecured, 12-month term (extendable by up to 12 months), prepayable without penalty. May also use existing term loan and RCF.
  • Classified as a significant transaction under UKLR 7.3.1R/7.3.2R but not subject to shareholder approval.
  • CEO Michael Murray (who sits on HUGO BOSS supervisory board) recused himself from the Board's discussion and decision.
  • Rationale: HUGO BOSS described as "one of the top five brands" across the Group; Frasers remains supportive of Chair Stephan Sturm and CEO Daniel Grieder's sustainable growth strategy.
  • HUGO BOSS FY25 financials cited: revenue €4,269.8m, EBITDA €781.5m, gross assets €3,721.2m, net assets €1,557.7m.
  • Pro forma combined 6-month EBITDA (to 26 Oct 2025): €971.3m / £848.1m (Frasers £448.6m + HUGO BOSS £399.5m equivalent).
  • Pro forma accounting impact: goodwill of €1,117.5m (£975.7m) would be recognised; total liabilities would rise by €1,999.0m (£1,745.4m) including €21.0m transaction costs.
  • Revaluation of existing stake at €38.00 would trigger a €3.7m (£3.2m) charge to the income statement immediately prior to completion.
  • Frasers had no access to HUGO BOSS management or non-public information — assessment based solely on public data, flagged as a key risk.
  • Advisers: BNP Paribas and Deutsche Bank (financial); RPC (English law); Gleiss Lutz (German law).
  • No significant change in Frasers' financial position since 26 October 2025.

body:
• Maiden mineral resource estimate for portions of Motapa expected to be published in Q3 2026.
  • Drilling confirmed continuity of mineralisation along a strike length of ~6km within the Bubi Greenstone Belt, with multiple shear zones across Motapa North, Central and South, and both oxide and sulphide mineralisation.
  • Motapa lies directly adjacent to the Bilboes Gold Project (proven & probable reserves of 1.75Moz gold in 24.1Mt at 2.26g/t), enabling potential shared infrastructure and reduced capital intensity.
  • 2025 programme: 22,364m trenching, 1,561.78m DD and 18,547m RC drilling, focused on Motapa North sulphides and Mpudzi (Motapa Central) oxide/sulphide delineation.
  • Selected Motapa North high-grade intercepts: 19.00m at 8.08g/t (JPRC52); 6.38m at 13.95g/t (JDD11); 12.00m at 7.12g/t (JPRC63); 17.00m at 3.25g/t (JPRC51); 13.00m at 3.72g/t (PLV1RC10); 6.00m at 6.89g/t (PLV1RC15); 14.00m at 4.31g/t (PLV5RC4).
  • Motapa Central (Mpudzi) highlights: 7.00m at 2.39g/t (MPZRC79); 3.00m at 4.79g/t (MPZRC64); 2.00m at 5.25g/t (MPZRC117) — oxide mineralisation confirmed to depths of ~35m, supporting near-term development optionality.
  • Motapa North mineralised zones display pinch-and-swell geometry with true widths from ~0.5m up to 17.1m (JPRC52).
  • Historic oxide pits at Motapa North sit only ~250m south of the Bilboes property boundary, close to the planned Bilboes metallurgical facility — supporting integration thesis.
  • 2026 programme will include infill drilling and testing of gap areas between Pluvious 123/Pluvious 4 pits and between Jupiter/Shawl pits, plus increased activity at Motapa South.
  • QAQC: overall CRM compliance rate of 92.2%; underperformance of standard AMIS0786 (43.6% pass) flagged for further investigation; blanks 97.1% pass rate.
  • CEO Mark Learmonth: "While our immediate focus remains the development of Bilboes, targeting first gold in Q4 2028, Motapa represents a compelling opportunity to extend mine life and increase future production across a combined mining complex."
  • Mining lease covers ~2,200 hectares; tenure provides both exploration and mining rights, located 110km north of Bulawayo, Zimbabwe.

body:
• ROM deliveries from Molefe Mine to the Sable refinery have recommenced following successful Pit 2 expansion under the updated mine plan combining Pits 2 and 3.
  • Ramp-up profile: ~6,000tpm in June, ~8,500tpm by August, steady-state 10,000tpm by October 2026 — equating to >100% increase in ROM deliveries to Sable.
  • Post pit integration, Molefe targets a step-up from ~12,000t/quarter HG ROM to >30,000t/quarter HG Cu reef ore delivered to Sable.
  • Combined mined copper reef set to reach 60,000t per quarter post Pit 2+3 combination, at an average stripping ratio of 6:1.
  • Accelerated pre-strip programme (started April 2026) remains on track for completion in July 2026.
  • Next development phase: (i) on-site ore sorting and processing for better HG/LG segregation and improved recovery; (ii) resource definition drilling across the greater Molefe district and additional exploration properties.
  • JORC-compliant resource / competent person's report targeted for Q4 CY2026, subject to assay timing (following Phase 2 drilling).
  • Ramp-up will use both newly mined ROM and strategic stockpiled material during the transition to integrated on-site ore sorting/processing.
  • CEO Leon Coetzer: "Molefe Mine is evolving into a cornerstone asset within our integrated mine-to-metals platform, with the operation on track to achieve a meaningful step-up in production over the coming months."
  • CEO on strategy: "Our strategy is to mine while we explore, expanding both production and the resource base simultaneously... we are establishing a blueprint that we believe can be replicated across multiple copper opportunities within the region."
  • Group target reiterated: 25,000 tpa copper production via three-pillar strategy (Roan concentrator, Sable refinery + regional mining, Large Waste Rock Project).
  • Live investor presentation scheduled for 10 June 2026, 14:00 UK time via Investor Meet Company.

body:
• Recommended cash acquisition of Tate & Lyle by Ingredion via scheme of arrangement, unanimously recommended by Tate & Lyle Board.
  • Cash consideration of 595p per share, plus permitted dividends of up to 13.2p (FY26 final) and 6.8p (H1 FY27 interim) = total headline value up to 615p per share.
  • Values Tate & Lyle equity at ~£2.7bn ($3.6bn) on cash consideration alone, or ~£2.8bn including permitted dividends; implied enterprise value £3.7bn–£3.8bn ($5.0bn).
  • Headline premium of ~64.0% to undisturbed closing price (13 May 2026), 70.8% to 3-month VWAP, 67.0% to 6-month VWAP.
  • Implied EV/Adjusted EBITDA multiple of ~9.1x (including permitted dividends) / ~8.8x pre-synergy on cash consideration.
  • Initial unsolicited proposal was 530p (80% cash / 20% Ingredion stock) — rejected; deal reached after four further proposals, now all-cash.
  • Irrevocable undertakings secured for 17.1% of share capital, including 16.8% from Huber Equity Corporation (75m shares) and 0.3% from directors.
  • Huber may sell up to 100% of its stake after the earlier of receiving the 2027 Interim Dividend or 1 February 2027 (post-Meetings), with restrictions on transfers to competing bidders.
  • Huber undertaking terminates if a competing offer exceeds the total value by ≥10%.
  • Scheme expected to become Effective in H2 2027, subject to Material Antitrust Conditions in EU, Brazil, Canada, China, Colombia, Mexico, South Korea, Tanzania, UK, US and Zanzibar.
  • Long Stop Date: 8 December 2027 (extendable to 8 June 2028).
  • Financing: $4.225bn JPMorgan bridge facility in place; FX option taken to hedge GBP payment; final funding via cash, new debt and bridge drawdown if needed.
  • Combined Group: ~$9.9bn revenue, $1.8bn adjusted EBITDA, headquartered at Ingredion's Westchester, Illinois office; Jim Zallie to continue as Chairman & CEO.
  • Run-rate net cost synergies of ~$130m by end-2030 (~60% SG&A, ~40% COGS); one-off costs ~$175m.
  • Expected to be >15% accretive to adjusted EPS in first full fiscal year after Effective Date.
  • Pro forma net debt/EBITDA ~3x at close, falling to ~2.5x within 18 months; commitment to preserve investment grade rating.
  • Potential ~3% workforce reduction in the Combined Group post-completion review (corporate, manufacturing, support overlap).
  • £18m cash retention award pool for ~100 Tate & Lyle employees; CEO Nick Hampton and CFO Sarah Kuijlaars receive cash retention of 150% and 125% of base salary respectively (within the £18m pool).
  • Tate & Lyle to be de-listed from LSE and re-registered as a private company post-completion; ADS programme to be terminated.
  • Tate & Lyle FY26 results (already reported 21 May 2026): revenue down 3%, pro forma Adjusted EBITDA down 3%; over $50m productivity savings delivered; 5-year productivity target raised by $50m to $200m by FY28; CP Kelco $50m synergy target met a year early.
  • FY27 outlook reiterated: modest revenue growth (volume-led, H2-weighted) and broadly flat EBITDA before ~$20m hit from rescheduling bio-gums capacity consolidation.
  • David Hearn, Chair of Tate & Lyle: "The Board of Tate & Lyle believes Ingredion's offer represents an attractive opportunity for shareholders to crystallise value in cash, and that it will be an excellent steward of Tate & Lyle."
  • Jim Zallie, Ingredion Chair & CEO: "Combining Ingredion and Tate & Lyle's complementary portfolios creates a global leader in ingredient solutions with the expertise and geographic reach to help shape the future of food."
  • Board candidly acknowledged FY26 performance was "disappointing" and that continued challenging market conditions create risk to timing of delivering its financial algorithm — a key factor in recommending the deal.
  • Tate & Lyle shares closed +14.77% at 564p on 8 June 2026, still ~5% below the 595p cash terms (~8% below the 615p headline), reflecting timing/regulatory risk to H2 2027 close.

body:
• Roan annual maintenance shutdown completed in May 2026; operations resumed at full capacity targeting 30,000tpm ROM throughput.
  • New fine copper concentrate dewatering circuit commissioning completed; fine-tuning underway for stable continuous operations.
  • Fines concentrate stream represents ~25.5% of contained copper in total ROM feed to Roan; circuit has demonstrated capacity above current fines production levels.
  • Roan holds significant stocks of naturally dried fine concentrate available for transport to Sable to buffer any interruptions.
  • Monthly fines concentrate contains ~140t of copper previously stockpiled at Roan.
  • Copper oxide flotation circuit upgraded during shutdown, targeting ~5% improvement in copper recoveries to partly offset cost inflation.
  • Local fuel prices up ~80%, directly impacting ROM and concentrate transport costs.
  • Acid consumption ~20% and transport ~16% of monthly expenditure — flagged as key cost pressures.
  • Optional front-end DMS circuit to further increase Roan throughput under consideration during June 2026.
  • Updated copper production guidance deferred until steady-state performance across integrated Roan-Sable circuit is demonstrated.
  • May production was impacted by the planned shutdown; June 2026 expected to give clearer read on sustainable run-rate and recoveries.
  • CEO Leon Coetzer: "The successful progression of the Roan dewatering circuit through commissioning and ramp-up marks another important milestone in the expansion of our Zambia copper operations."
  • CEO on flexibility: "The ability to process both newly generated fine concentrate material together with the historical stockpile provides increased operational flexibility and supports the continued scaling of our integrated copper strategy."
  • Group strategic target reiterated: 25,000tpa copper production via Roan concentrator, Sable refinery and Large Waste Rock Project.

body:
• Ag Economy Barometer fell to 119 in May, down from 121 in April.
  • Current Conditions Index dropped 8 points to its lowest level since December 2024; Future Expectations Index rose 1 point.
  • High input costs cited as top concern by a record 51% of respondents; 46% said input costs are limiting financial improvement this year.
  • Only 14% reported their farm is better off financially than a year ago; 22% expect improvement over the next 12 months.
  • Farm Capital Investment Index fell 3 points to 41, lowest since September 2024, signalling reduced appetite for large investments.
  • ~two-thirds expect 2026 net farm income to be reduced.
  • Among 2025 corn planters: ~50% expect break-even prices up to 6% higher; 30% expect break-even prices up 10%+.
  • Labour: 39% hire nonfamily workers; of those, 44% report some/a lot of difficulty hiring in 2026.
  • AI adoption scepticism: 59% say AI tools would not improve their labour/equipment situation; 37% a little; only 4% a lot.
  • Farmland value expectations rose despite weaker current sentiment: Short-Term Index 121→130; Long-Term Index 155→160.
  • "Right direction" sentiment for the U.S. fell to 52% in May, the lowest since the question began (July 2025), vs ~71% average in H2 2025.
  • Sharp divergence in 5-year outlook: only 31% expect good times for crop producers vs 68% for livestock producers.
  • Quote — Michael Langemeier (principal investigator): "The persistence of high input costs is especially challenging in an environment where many producers are already operating with tighter margins."
  • Quote — Langemeier: "When producers see fewer opportunities to improve their financial position despite strong operational management, it tends to weigh heavily on perceptions of current conditions and investment plans."

time_period: FY26 (year ending 30 June 2026) operational update, with FY27 guidance
body:
• Record annual gold production of ~275,000oz, up ~40% YoY (FY25: 196,527oz), landing at the low end of FY26 guidance range (275,000–292,000oz).
  • H2 FY26 production ~147,000oz, up ~14% vs H1 (128,296oz).
  • Strong contributions from Elikhulu, MTR, Evander and Barberton underground offset slower-than-expected ramp-up at Tennant Mines (Australia).
  • FY26 AISC expected at top end of guidance ~US$1,870/oz (US$/ZAR 17.00), despite inflationary pressures; Group remains fully unhedged.
  • Projected cash position of ~US$220m at FY26 year-end; Group now in net cash position (vs net debt of US$46.2m at 31 Dec 2025); only outstanding debt is DMTNs of US$49.7m.
  • Cash impacted by US$10.3m strategic investment in CuFe Limited and US$7.0m to secure strategic cyanide supplies.
  • FY27 production guidance: 280,000–302,000oz at AISC US$2,075–US$2,175/oz (US$/ZAR 17.00) — note material AISC step-up (~11–16% vs FY26) reflecting above-inflation cost increases for reagents, electricity and key inputs.
  • FY27 capex guidance raised to US$324m from US$267m previously (US$282m expansion + US$42m sustaining), driven by accelerated White Devil development, Nobles plant crusher/filter belt, fast-tracked exploration and finalised renewable energy project costs.
  • FY26 capex forecast US$180m, including US$10m for White Devil, ~US$8m Tennant solar plant, ~US$3m for Soweto Cluster DFS.
  • Tennant Mines (Australia): FY26 production ~34,000oz; FY26H2 ~18,500oz (+19% vs H1); head grade lifted to ~1.5g/t (H1: 1.3g/t); Q4 annualised run-rate ~45,000oz; FY27 guidance 48,000–52,000oz with target of ~100,000oz p.a. within three years.
  • White Devil open pit: Indicated Resource >3Mt at 3.73g/t (378koz); Juno 1.96Mt at 4.16g/t (262koz); Golden Forty 0.5Mt at 7.25g/t (114koz) — to underpin Tennant production over next five years.
  • MTR: FY26H2 ~30,500oz, FY26 ~52,000oz; calcine layer continues to impact grade/recoveries, expected to be mined through in Q1 FY27, after which production forecast >60,000oz/year.
  • Soweto Cluster DFS on track for completion by June 2026 — potential 600ktpm standalone facility producing ~30,000–35,000oz p.a. over 15-year LOM.
  • MTR expansion study for hard rock circuit could add a further 20,000–30,000oz p.a.
  • Elikhulu: FY26 production >56,500oz (FY25: 52,606oz) — highest since FY20.
  • Evander underground: FY26 ~47,000oz, +68% YoY; recovered grade jumped to >11g/t (FY25: 6.8g/t) on 8 Shaft reaching 24 Level B-Raise.
  • Barberton underground: FY26 ~72,000oz (FY25: 68,550oz), +5% YoY.
  • BTRP: FY26 ~13,000oz (FY25: 15,224oz); US$5.9m flotation circuit approved (completion end-2026) to improve recoveries and enable refractory ore treatment.
  • Emmerson Resources acquisition (Tennant Creek consolidation): Scheme Meeting 15 June 2026, implementation 1 July 2026; Pan African will undertake an ASX listing as part of the transaction.
  • Acquired 15% stake in ASX-listed CuFe for ~A$15.35m on 19 May 2026 to unlock synergies with Group's Warrego copper-gold project.
  • Middle East contingency: rolling three-month cyanide supply secured at South African operations; one-month on-site diesel storage at Tennant Mines.
  • Final results scheduled for ~16 September 2026.
  • CEO Cobus Loots: "It has been an exceptional year for Pan African Resources, with the Group set to achieve its record gold production target, increasing gold output by some 40% year-on-year. Financially, the Group has never been in a stronger position."

body:
• CEO Andrew Knott to acquire 128,550,000 existing Ordinary Shares (~6% of issued share capital) from the Savannah Energy 2022 Trust (EBT) for aggregate consideration of ~£8.74m.
  • Acquisition takes Knott's aggregate interest in the Company to ~20% of issued share capital, made via wholly-owned vehicle Lothian Capital Partners 6 Limited.
  • Purchase price of 6.8p per share, equal to the middle market closing price on Friday 29 May 2026 (i.e. no premium).
  • Non-dilutive secondary acquisition — no new shares issued, no treasury/cancellation activity by the Company.
  • Payment structure: ~£1.75m Initial Consideration in cash on Completion, balance deferred and payable in cash over 6 years, with 6% p.a. interest (~£420k annual interest payments); deferred balance due on 6th anniversary.
  • Purchaser has the option to settle some/all of the final deferred amount by transferring Savannah ordinary shares (at market value) to the Trust.
  • Knott has provided a personal guarantee to the EBT for the deferred consideration plus an asset and liability letter to the Trustee.
  • Purchaser has 50 business days from 30 May 2026 to pay the Initial Consideration; shares transfer on payment.
  • EBT currently holds 205,701,993 Ordinary Shares (was issued 210m new shares on 22 October 2025).
  • Cancellation of all Knott's outstanding options over 38,347,622 Ordinary Shares for nil consideration, conditional on Completion — 21,312,418 over EBT-held shares and 17,035,204 over unissued shares — reducing future dilution risk.
  • Relationship Agreement entered into with Knott and his vehicles, providing minority shareholder/governance protections: arm's length related-party dealings, related party voting restrictions, commitment to maintain at least two independent Directors, AIM Rules compliance.
  • Board nomination rights: at ≥20% but <27.5% holding, right to nominate one Director but only if Knott is not himself a Director; at ≥27.5%, right to nominate one Director if Knott is a Director, or up to two if he is not — capping additional representation while Knott remains CEO.
  • Governance/representation provisions suspend if Knott's aggregate holding falls below 20%, reinstated if threshold re-met.
  • Company framing: transaction "significantly increase[s] Mr Knott's ownership interest in Savannah, further strengthening his alignment with the Company's long-term shareholders."
  • Board rationale on option cancellation: "in the best interests of shareholders as a whole, as it reduces potential future dilution and simplifies Mr Knott's long-term economic alignment with shareholders by replacing option-based economics with a materially increased direct equity interest."

body:
• Commissioning started on the US$1.5 billion AP60 smelter expansion at Complexe Arvida, Quebec, with start-up beginning in March and full ramp of all 96 new pots expected by end-2026.
  • Adds ~160,000 tpa of primary aluminium capacity, bringing total AP60 output to 220,000 tpa.
  • AP60 expansion plus the planned Arvida recycling centre will more than offset closure of the older Arvida potrooms, with shutdown expected to complete in June.
  • Carbon footprint: ~1.6 t CO2e/t aluminium vs 3.2t at old Arvida and 10.9t industry average; combined with hydropower, ~1/6 of industry-average emissions.
  • Expected ~290,000 tonnes/year CO2 reduction vs the old Arvida smelter, plus up to 90% reduction in fine particulate matter.
  • Described as the first major primary aluminium project in the West in more than a decade.
  • Supports ~100 permanent local jobs; peak construction created 1,500+ jobs and generated >C$1 billion in economic benefits for Quebec.
  • Linked to ELYSIS partnership demonstration plant in Quebec (carbon-free smelting, oxygen by-product) — AP60 is the first licence of the breakthrough technology.
  • Jérôme Pécresse (CEO Aluminium & Lithium): "Rio Tinto is now strongly positioned for decades to come with one of the most advanced smelting technologies operating at commercial scale."
  • Premier Christine Fréchette flagged the backdrop of "economic uncertainty related to U.S. tariffs", framing the project as securing Quebec's aluminium future.

body:
• Article is a sector piece on AI executives walking back job-loss warnings; Standard Chartered referenced as a recent corporate example.
  • STAN announced last week plans to cut thousands of jobs by 2030, with AI replacing staff in a range of administrative roles.
  • Context: Snap cut ~1,000 jobs last month citing AI-driven efficiency gains.
  • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang pushed back on CEOs blaming AI for layoffs: "The narrative that connects AI to job loss, for many of the CEOs that are doing it – it is just too lazy."
  • Huang: "How is it possible that AI became productive and useful only six months ago, and they were somehow laying people off two years ago because of AI? It doesn't make any sense."
  • Huang: "It was just a way for them to sound smart, and I really hate that. I think we're scaring people and that's irresponsible."
  • OpenAI's Sam Altman conceded at CBA's Accelerate AI Conference in Sydney that there has been no "jobs apocalypse," saying: "I thought there would have been more impact on entry-level white-collar jobs being eliminated by now than has actually happened… that is an area where my intuitions were just off."
  • Anthropic's Dario Amodei softened tone: even if 90% of jobs are automated, the remaining 10% of human workers would be vastly more productive.
  • Reversals from Altman and Amodei coincide with expected high-profile IPOs at OpenAI and Anthropic requiring broad investor buy-in.
  • Fed Governor Lisa Cook warned full AI employment effects may still lie ahead: "We could be approaching the most significant reorganization of work in generations," noting job losses could precede gains.
  • ECB and most economic institutions say AI has had only minor employment effects so far.
  • Read-across for STAN: its 2030 AI-driven headcount plan stands out against a narrative shift where leading AI CEOs are now downplaying near-term displacement, potentially increasing scrutiny of the bank's stated AI productivity rationale.

• Shares fell 5.2% to 483.00p on Tuesday morning following the chemical incident update.
  • Issue identified Thursday in a tank storing methyl methacrylate at GKN Aerospace's Garden Grove, California site; described as "a thermal issue".
  • Methyl methacrylate is a flammable irritant (used in plastics) that can cause respiratory/neurological reactions, prompting mandatory evacuation orders affecting ~50,000 people (per AFP).
  • No active leak, no injuries, no contamination confirmed by authorities on Monday evening; continuous live atmospheric monitoring in place.
  • Tank pressure declining; temperature fell to ~34°C from 38°C on Monday.
  • Evacuation zone reduced after consultation with technical specialists, emergency services and authorities, though ~16,000 people remain impacted.
  • Management statement: "GKN is working closely with customers on operational recovery and supply plans" — flagging potential aerospace supply chain disruption risk.
  • Garden Grove Police Chief Amir El-Farra: "Please understand that we are doing this for your safety, and we will continue to work diligently."

body:
• Chair Albert Manifold removed as chair and director, with BP citing "serious concerns" raised to the board "related to important governance standards, oversight and conduct."
  • Shares fell 5.2% to 522.70p on the news; closed -4.03% at 529.00p.
  • Director Ian Tyler appointed interim chair, effective immediately; Tyler also chairs Grafton Group PLC. Permanent succession process to be initiated.
  • Manifold had only been chair since October (joined board September) — tenure of roughly eight months.
  • Second major executive removal for conduct reasons in three years (after CEO Bernard Looney in 2023).
  • Senior Independent Director Amanda Blanc: "Albert has helped bring a welcome focus and pace to bp's transformation. However, the board has been surprised and disappointed to learn of governance oversight and conduct issues it deems unacceptable and has taken decisive action."
  • Manifold credited with reversing BP's renewables push, boosting oil & gas investment, and orchestrating the removal of former CEO Murray Auchincloss, replaced by Meg O'Neill.
  • Reportedly clashed with CEO Meg O'Neill; survived a shareholder rebellion last month.
  • Interim Chair Tyler on O'Neill: "She has already taken bold action to simplify and strengthen the organization such as announcing the move to a clearly defined upstream/downstream model. Under her leadership we are building a simpler, stronger, more valuable bp."
  • Analyst reaction — Citi (Syme): reasons for dismissal "are, in our view, moot"; flags that Manifold "was part of the equity story" and many investors "were re-engaging in the equity story because of his driving of change"; key question is whether the investment pathway is "now largely set."
  • Morningstar (Stewart): BP has "the most volatile boardroom of the oil supermajors"; corporate governance "must a priority of the interim chair and his eventual successor."
  • XTB (Brooks): raises "genuine concerns about HR policies at BP, and the corporate culture"; questions how breaches "weren't unearthed during the hiring process"; risk that the pivot back to oil & gas could be threatened or delayed.
  • RBC Capital Markets: if underperformance continues, "BP shares would become more attractive for a potential acquirer" — explicit takeover speculation angle.
  • Near-term read-through: derails BP's YTD catch-up versus oil & gas peers, though could give O'Neill room to accelerate her strategic agenda.

  • Pretax profit +7.6% to £1.44bn (vs £1.05bn), boosted by lower depreciation and amortisation.
  • Revenue -3.5% to £19.65bn (vs £20.36bn), narrowly below £19.68bn consensus; dragged by lower International revenue, handset trading declines and weaker adjusted UK service revenue.
  • Adjusted UK service revenue -0.8% to £15.45bn, beating £15.38bn consensus; lower voice volumes offset by CPI-linked price rises and improved Openreach FTTP mix.
  • Adjusted EBITDA £8.23bn vs £8.21bn (consensus £8.21bn).
  • Free cash flow slipped to £1.51bn from £1.60bn.
  • Openreach broadband line losses 825,000 for FY26 (Q4: 203,000), better than 850,000 guidance; FY27 losses guided to ~800,000.
  • Record FTTP build of 4.8m premises passed; 2.2m net FTTP adds; now reaches more than two-thirds of UK homes/businesses, on track for 25m milestone by end-December.
  • Final dividend +1.9% to 5.87p; total FY26 DPS 8.32p, +2.0%, in line with consensus.
  • New dividend policy: low-to-mid single digit growth from FY27 onwards until "metrics consistent with a BBB+ credit rating are reached"; thereafter "residual cash flow will be available for enhanced distributions to shareholders".
  • JPMorgan pushed back credit-rating-driven re-rating by one year but maintains DPS doubling to 18p by March 2031; flags upside risk as forecast £1.6bn FY31 dividend is just 50% of residual pre-pension equity FCF.

body:
• BP is facing a lawsuit in Kenya over alleged toxic waste dumping in Kargi and Kalacha villages in Marsabit County, with hundreds of petitioners alleging contamination killed thousands of livestock and caused cancer in locals.
  • Liability stems from BP's 1998 acquisition of US oil firm Amoco, which conducted the 1984–1990 oil exploration; BP did not carry out the original activity.
  • Petitioners' lawyer Kelvin Kubai: "British Petroleum has been sued in respect of the legacy activities of Amoco Corporation" and by acquiring Amoco "it assumes both liabilities and assets".
  • Court papers indicate ~200 petitioners, mostly cancer sufferers, have already died and are now represented by family members.
  • Kubai characterised the situation as "environmental genocide," warning numbers could rise.
  • Supporting evidence cited includes a University of Nairobi study finding nitrates 5–10x WHO recommended levels in drinking water, and a January 2020 incident in Kargi where ~7,000 livestock reportedly died in one day.
  • Documents were formally served via the UK foreign affairs ministry on Thursday after BP had disputed service on procedural grounds.
  • Court mention set for 16 June to confirm receipt of documents; BP has yet to comment.
  • No financial quantum disclosed; shares were up 0.4% at 566.10p on Thursday afternoon (note: article close price shown at 551.20p, -2.48%).

• Smackover Lithium (55% Standard Lithium / 45% Equinor JV) has signed an EPCM agreement with Wood Group USA for the upstream well field of the South West Arkansas (SWA) Project, ahead of FID.
  • Well field scope: 4 well pads, 12 supply wells, 10 injection wells, brine gathering/return pipelines to the Central Processing Facility, plus a gas gathering system to a disposal well.

  • Upstream well field accounts for less than one-third of total Project capex (per the DFS filed 15 October 2025).

  • Project continues to receive support from the US DOE Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation (award DE-MS0000099).

  • CEO Mike Duffy: "He has an impressive track record in field-based, recurring service operations, making him the ideal leader to drive our North American business forward."

body:
• EPRA EPS up 63.5% to 8.5p; ahead of consensus (compiled 7.9p; Visible Alpha 7.9p).
  • EPRA NTA/share 524p, up 6.1% (vs consensus 522-523p); IFRS profit after tax £154.5m (vs £116.0m).

  • Rental values +5.8% LFL (offices +6.3%, prime offices +7.2%, retail +1.6%).
  • FY27 rental growth guidance: 4.0%-7.0%; prime offices 4.0%-8.0% (matches FY26 guidance range delivered).
  • Total dividend raised to 8.2p (final 5.3p, payable 10 July 2026); ROE 7.9%, progressing toward >10% FY27 target.
  • Record leasing year: 88 new leases/renewals at £70.9m p.a., 10.3% above March 2025 ERV; rent roll up 46% LFL to £153.6m, with further organic growth potential of 95%.
  • Rent reviews settled at +30.1% over previous rent and 9.0% ahead of ERV (incl. KKR and Glencore at Hanover Square).
  • Vacancy rate 6.0% (2025: 5.9%); customer retention 76%; AI-led businesses now c.11% of portfolio (27% of Fully Managed).
  • Capital recycling: £490m of disposals at 2.3% premium to book (£1,251 psf), incl. 1 Newman Street (£250m, largest West End deal of 2025), wells&more (£172m), Challenger House (£42m), 103/113 Regent St JV share (£26m).
  • Acquisitions: £69m at just £592 psf (The Gable £18m at 6.4% NIY; 10 South Crescent £51m at 6.8% NIY) adding to Fitzrovia cluster.
  • £200m of further sales under consideration; potential £1.0bn+ over medium term.
  • 2 Aldermanbury Square completed on time/budget, 100% pre-let to Clifford Chance.
  • Three HQ schemes on-site c.50% pre-let (CD&R at 30 Duke Street at 6.5% above ERV with projected 37.1% profit on cost; Quantexa 52,300 sq ft at The Delft).
  • The Delft costs increased by £14m due to supply chain insolvencies; profit on cost now 20.7% (vs prior expectations), IRR 12.0%, yield 7.6%.
  • Three Fully Managed deliveries in year (c.77,000 sq ft); 141 Wardour Street fully let within two months at £279 psf; 170 Piccadilly 73% let/under offer at £294 psf (highest in portfolio).
  • £116m committed capex remaining on three on-site HQ schemes; £223m capex to come across five on-site schemes; total programme expected surplus £131m at current rents/yields, rising to £260m on 10% rental growth.
  • Three pipeline HQ schemes incl. planning secured at St Thomas Yard SE1; total combined committed+pipeline capex £484m for 601,300 sq ft.
  • Fully Managed target of 1m sq ft (currently 654,000 sq ft committed, c.31% of offices).
  • New £525m five-year ESG-linked RCF signed October 2025 at 105bps over SONIA (replacing £450m facility + repaying £75m term loan at 175bps); Moody's Baa2 confirmed.
  • EPRA LTV 28.6% (vs 30.8%); cash & undrawn facilities £411.9m; WAULT debt maturity 5.4 years; weighted avg cost of debt 5.0% (down from 5.2%).
  • Property values would need to fall 45% before covenant breach.
  • 65% of drawn debt at fixed/hedged rates (down from 85% after £200m cap expired Oct 2025).
  • Revenue £117.9m (vs £94.2m); Fully Managed revenue up 128% to £42.8m; Fully Managed NOI £18.0m (+125%).
  • Cost of sales rose to £49.3m (from £35.1m), driven by Fully Managed service expense scaling.
  • Admin costs £44.2m (+£4.2m), incl. £1.6m new finance/property system go-live late 2026 and external whistleblower investigation costs.
  • Gross finance costs £48.6m (+£9.0m); capitalised interest £37.7m (+£11.2m).
  • Three customers entered administration (1.1% of rent roll); 99.3% of rents collected within 7 days.
  • CBRE rotated off as valuer; Knight Frank appointed for first valuation at 30 September 2026 (RICS mandatory rotation).
  • Two internal promotions to ExCo focused on Flex and customer experience.
  • CEO Toby Courtauld: "I am pleased to report on a year of numerous operational successes... EPS was up by 63% and net assets grew by 6.1%, with development values up 22%."
  • CEO outlook: "Whilst the external environment remains volatile, we are well positioned to build on this momentum; demand for our premium HQ and Flex spaces is strong and our pipeline is long, concentrated in the most sought-after, core locations."
  • Market context: only 2.9m sq ft of speculative supply expected annually over next four years vs ~4.5m sq ft take-up.

body:
• Reported revenue £19.7bn, down 3%; adjusted revenue £19.6bn, down 4%, hit by International divestments, handset declines and lower adjusted UK service revenue.
  • Adjusted UK service revenue £15.4bn, down 1% (voice volume drag offset by CPI-linked price rises and FTTP mix).
  • Adjusted EBITDA £8.23bn, flat YoY; like-for-like (ex-divestments) up 1%; landed at top of £8.2-8.3bn guidance.
  • Reported PBT £1.44bn, up 8%; adjusted basic EPS 18.3p, down 3%.
  • Normalised free cash flow £1.5bn, down 6% (higher capex/interest, absence of prior-year tax refund); in line with c.£1.5bn guide.
  • Capex £5.13bn, up 6% (FTTP build/provisioning), slightly above c.£5.0bn guide.
  • Net debt £20.0bn vs £19.8bn; IAS 19 pension deficit widened to £4.2bn from £4.1bn.
  • Final dividend 5.87p (+2%); full-year DPS 8.32p (+2%).
  • New dividend policy: low-to-mid single digit annual growth in FY27+ until BBB+ credit metrics reached, after which residual cash flow available for enhanced shareholder distributions (i.e. potential buybacks signalled).
  • FY27 guidance: adjusted revenue £19.0-19.5bn; UK service revenue £15.1-15.4bn (includes c.£150-200m voice/PSTN headwind); adjusted EBITDA growth to £8.2-8.3bn; capex ex-spectrum c.£4.3bn (down ~£0.8bn); NFCF c.£2.0bn.
  • Mid-term: capex ex-spectrum to fall by >£1bn from FY26 level by end of decade; NFCF reiterated at c.£3.0bn by FY30.
  • Transformation target raised to £3.7bn from £3.0bn, extended one year to FY30; cost to achieve rises to £1.4bn from £1.0bn.
  • £580m gross annualised savings in FY26 at £336m cost; £1.5bn total savings over two years at £0.8bn cost; headcount down 7% to 108k; network energy use -6%; Openreach repair volumes -18%.
  • Openreach FTTP build: record 4.8m premises added; footprint 23m (>2/3 of UK); on track for 25m by December 2026.
  • Openreach FTTP net adds 2.2m; total connected 8.8m; take-up rate >38%; broadband ARPU +4% to £16.7.
  • Openreach broadband line losses 825k for FY (Q4: 203k), better than c.850k guide; FY27 losses guided to c.800k.
  • EE 5G+ population coverage 73%, up from 43%; retail FTTP base +31% YoY to 4.5m; 5G base +10% to 14.5m.
  • Consumer returned to customer growth: +26k broadband, +104k postpaid mobile, +72k TV; but broadband ARPU -1% to £41.7 and mobile ARPU -1% to £19.3 in competitive market; convergence up to 26.6% (from 24.6%).
  • Business: new wins with BAE Systems, NIE Networks, easyJet; sovereign AI data centre partnership with Nscale.
  • International: five non-core divestments completed; revenue -15%, EBITDA -29%, FCF -£117m (vs -£34m).
  • Segment EBITDA: Openreach £4.23bn (+5%), Consumer £2.60bn (-2%), Business £1.27bn (-5%), International £145m (-29%).
  • Group NPS at record 33.4, +4.1pts YoY.
  • BT brand reintroduced with new Consumer and Business products in May 2026.
  • CEO Allison Kirkby: "We have delivered on our financial guidance and we are transforming ahead of plan, offsetting headwinds while successfully competing."
  • CEO on cash inflection: "reiterating our guidance of sustained growth, including cash flow inflection to c. £2.0bn in FY27 and to c. £3.0bn by the end of the decade."

• Headline LBT widened to £(552)m vs £(394)m in H1 FY25; reported LBT £(552)m vs £(401)m — in line with 16 April trading update.

  • RASK +1% YoY (Q2 +3% aided by route maturity, FX, earlier Easter); revenue per seat +5% to £73.36.
  • Total headline CASK +5% YoY; CASK ex-fuel +8% (inflation, resilience measures annualisation, digital investment, wet-lease for Italian bases, legal provisions); fuel CASK -5% on favourable hedging (avg jet fuel $726/MT, -8% YoY).

  • H2 FY26 CASK ex-fuel guided to low single-digit increase; fuel 72% hedged at $726/MT vs spot ~$1,350/MT; every $100/MT move = c.£35m fuel cost.
  • Short-term additional fuel hedging temporarily suspended given elevated near-term prices; minimum ticket fares raised; discretionary cost under review.
  • FY26 seat capacity growth 3% (H1 4%, H2 2%); ASK +6% (H1 8%, H2 5%); H1 FY27 capacity growth to moderate after 33% H1 ASK growth over three years.
  • All A319s to be retired by FY29 (accelerated), delivering c.£250m incremental annual cost efficiencies across FY27 & FY28.
  • Fleet 356 aircraft; 86% of A320neo family owned; order book 287 aircraft + 100 purchase rights; gross capex guidance: c.£1.7bn FY26, c.£2.3bn FY27, c.£3.3bn FY28.

  • Holidays customers expected to grow low double digits in FY26 from 3.1m base; H2 FY26 76% sold.

  • Medium-term target reiterated: >£1bn PBT as conditions normalise.
  • On-time performance 78% (+1ppt); Airline CSAT 84% (+2ppt); Holidays CSAT 85% (+1ppt); 71% of bookings from returning customers; app now 38% of direct airline bookings.
  • Contingent liability: Spanish €29m hand-luggage fine appealed (bank guarantee posted); easyJet maintains policy is lawful; EC has opened infringement procedure against Spain.
  • CEO Kenton Jarvis: "easyJet is well placed to manage the current environment, supported by one of the strongest investment‑grade balance sheets in European aviation."

• Pretax profit down 29% to £364.6m (prior: £511.8m), hit by cyber attack disruption.
  • Adjusted pretax profit fell 24% to £671.4m (prior: £881.1m), beating Visible Alpha consensus of £640.3m.
  • Revenue: up 25% to £17.37bn (statutory £17.27bn) from £13.91bn.

  • Full-year dividend raised 17% to 4.2p (final 3.0p vs 2.6p) — signals confidence despite cyber hit.
  • Shares +2.1% to 333.8p on the day vs FTSE 100 -0.4%.
  • Described as a "year of two halves: significant operational impact from the cyber incident during the first, followed by a return to sales and profit growth in the second."
  • Food was the standout: adj. operating profit £444.5m (down from £491.8m) — H1 hit by higher markdown/waste, H2 saw sustained volume growth.
  • Fashion, Home & Beauty sales -7.7%; adj. operating profit collapsed to £213.4m from £478.0m (more than halved) due to pause in online trading post-cyber.
  • International sales -7.2%, with H2 improvement partly offset by Middle East shipment delays in the final month.
  • CEO Stuart Machin: "A resilient balance sheet supported by the hard work done on our cash position in recent years allowed us to absorb the cost of disruption without compromising our financial health."
  • Machin flagged a "triple whammy of headwinds" — "increased taxation, a greater regulatory burden and ongoing global conflict."
  • FHB recovery "has taken longer, but there is strong growth potential."
  • Outlook: profit growth "expected to resume" vs FY24/25, but no specific guidance figures given.
  • Cost headwinds cited: "higher fuel, freight and input costs and continued government tax levies and regulatory headwinds for the sector."
  • Mitigation via improved buying, value reinvestment to drive volume, and savings from structural cost reduction programme.

body:
• Climate resolution filed by 21 institutional investors led by Dutch group Follow This, calling for Shell to publish a strategy on creating shareholder value under a declining fossil fuel demand scenario, received 12.7% of investor votes (provisional).
  • Support fell from 20.6% in 2025 and a 30.5% peak in 2021, indicating waning momentum for climate shareholder activism at Shell.
  • Board, ISS and Glass Lewis all recommended voting against the resolution; Shell argued the issue is already covered in existing disclosures.
  • Chair Andrew Mackenzie on long-term outlook: "won't give you a single answer"; "where demand rises, our determination is to help meet it... Where the energy system is ready to change, we are ready to move with it."
  • CEO Wael Sawan said the resolution would "create a precedent for recurring single source scenario-based disclosure, which ultimately adds costs without helping our investors" and called it "damaging but duplicative".
  • Sawan reiterated strategy: "Shell's strategy has long been to secure oil and gas production that is advantaged on costs and carbon, offering us resilience in different demand scenarios."
  • Mackenzie confirmed hydrocarbons (oil and gas) remain central to all Shell scenarios, with decarbonisation focus on the *use* of hydrocarbons rather than exiting them.
  • Reference to Q1 record profits driven by oil price spike from the Iran war and ongoing Strait of Hormuz disruption — Sawan framed crisis as "another reminder of the fundamental importance of energy".
  • Shell has recently weakened several short- and medium-term climate targets citing transition uncertainty, but retains 2050 net zero ambition.
  • Follow This founder Mark van Baal flagged precedent risk: Shell cut dividends by 66% in 2020 when demand collapsed, warning of structural decline risk.
  • Mackenzie criticised shareholder resolutions as a debate mechanism, preferring direct engagement — signalling continued board resistance to AGM-led climate pressure.
  • Protest group Fossil Fuel London staged action outside HQ; references to pending London court cases from Philippines and Niger Delta communities over environmental impacts.
  • Shares +0.4% at 3,301.50p during the AGM session.

body:
• Anglo American agreed to sell its Australian steelmaking coal portfolio to Dhilmar Ltd for up to USD 3.88 billion in cash.
  • Structure: USD 2.3 billion upfront plus a price-linked earnout of up to USD 1.58 billion.
  • Deal expected to complete by Q1 2027; proceeds to be used to reduce net debt.
  • CEO Duncan Wanblad: "This agreement represents another major step in the simplification of our portfolio ahead of completing our merger with Teck. Through this transaction, we will complete our exit from steelmaking coal."
  • Portfolio sold includes 88% in Moranbah North & Grosvenor JVs, 70% in Capcoal JV, 86% in Roper Creek JV, 51% in Dawson/Dawson South/Theodore South JVs, and 50% in Moranbah South JV.
  • Dhilmar is a privately-held miner whose assets include the Eleonore gold mine in Canada, acquired from Newmont last year.
  • Arbitration with Peabody Energy continues over the November 2024 agreement to acquire the same portfolio; Anglo remains confident the Moranbah North incident did not constitute a material adverse change.
  • Moranbah North mine in Queensland was closed following an underground fire in March 2025 — the event Peabody relied on to terminate.
  • Separately, a Chile Second Environmental Tribunal ruling appears to overturn the 2021 environmental authorisation at the Collahuasi copper mine (Anglo 44%, Glencore 44%, Mitsui 12%).
  • Both owners say ruling is "limited to two specific aspects relating to analysis on the effects on a local community and on the marine environment" and neither expects "any immediate impact on production".
  • Market reaction: Anglo American -1.9% to 3,760p, Glencore -1.3% to 567.10p, vs FTSE 100 marginally higher.

• Revenue £209.1m, +2% (FY25: £204.5m); store revenue £207.6m, +2%.
  • Like-for-like store revenue £207.3m, +2%, driven entirely by rent (occupancy a drag).
  • Average achieved net rent per sq ft +4% to £35.98; closing net rent +3% to £36.28.
  • Closing occupancy 74.2%, down 4.5ppts (LfL down 1.7ppts to 77.0%); driven primarily by four new store openings adding 0.3m sq ft.
  • Post period-end, LfL occupancy gap has narrowed to 0.6ppts from 1.7ppts — key inflection management is flagging.
  • Store EBITDA £146.5m, +2%; margin flat at 70.5% despite occupancy headwind.
  • LfL operating cost inflation just 0.3% (vs +7% prior year); guiding to 2-3% LfL cost inflation in FY27 after absorbing a 9% rise in LfL property rates.
  • Adjusted PBT £117.5m, +2%; adjusted EPS 59.0p, +2%.
  • Statutory PBT £126.2m, -38% (FY25: £203.9m), purely due to lower revaluation surplus (£7.6m vs £79.7m).
  • Full-year dividend 47.2p, +2% (final 23.4p); entirely PID.
  • Net debt £476.7m (vs £388.7m), net debt/EBITDA 3.7x (up from 3.1x) — towards top of 3-4x target range.
  • Average cost of drawn debt down to 4.7% from 5.0% (peak 5.7% Sept 2023); 44% of drawn debt fixed.
  • Undrawn committed facilities of £83m; post period-end put in place a $225m Pricoa shelf facility (7-15yr fixed sterling notes, drawable in £10m tranches).
  • Interest cover 6.1x (flat); comfortably within covenants.
  • Capex £100.8m (vs £58.3m) on new store construction; capital commitments £54.3m at year-end.
  • Four new freehold stores opened: Staines (Jul'25), Queensbury (Oct'25), Slough Bath Road (Feb'26), Wembley (Mar'26). Queensbury, Slough Bath Road and Wembley currently loss-making at EBITDA level.
  • Pipeline: 12 development sites (~0.9m sq ft, 13% of MLA); 9 of 12 now have planning consent. Pipeline cost to complete £231m over 4 years, projected 8.3% return on capital, £39m NOI.
  • Property valuation £3,111m; like-for-like open store revaluation +0.5% (£15.7m uplift); IPUC revaluation deficit £8.1m on higher build costs. Exit cap rate unchanged at 5.5%.
  • Adjusted NAV 1,370.4p/share (vs 1,355.6p), +1%.
  • CEO transition: Jim Gibson to retire as CEO on 20 July 2026; COO John Hunter to succeed. Helen Gordon (CEO of Grainger) to join as SID from 1 June 2027.
  • Increased stake in Doncaster Security Operations Centre (DSOC) to 74% (from 34%) on 1 August 2025; now equity-accounted as JV.
  • Business customers now 36% of occupied space / 32% of revenue; first business occupancy growth (+16,000 sq ft H2) since early 2022.
  • Move-in mix: 40% home movers (23% owners, 17% renters); H1 was subdued post-Stamp Duty pull-forward, H2 improved after four BoE rate cuts in 2025.
  • Energy costs only 1.2% of revenue; solar capacity +13% to 9.6MW across 85 stores; energy pricing fixed to September 2026.
  • New customers paid 0.7% less than prior-year move-ins and 6.9% less than move-outs — implying revenue tailwind if occupancy gap closes.
  • Chairman Nicholas Vetch on outlook: "We recognise that the current operating environment presents considerable challenges for businesses across the sector, and we do not underestimate the headwinds that lie ahead."
  • CEO commentary noted activity stalled in March following "the start of the Iran war"; macro/geopolitical risks (Iran conflict, mortgage rates, US tariffs) explicitly flagged as drivers of softer activity in April/May 2025 and March 2026.

body:
• Launching an additional €500 million share buyback programme, following completion of the initial €500m tranche (final purchase 14 May 2026) under the €1.5bn total return of excess cash announced on 26 February 2026.
  • Purpose: reduce share capital via cancellation, subject to shareholder approval at AGM.
  • Programme runs 18 May 2026 to no later than 30 September 2026.
  • Split: €374m purchased from market participants and €126m from Qatar Airways on pro rata terms.
  • Qatar Airways participating to preserve its 25.1434% stake; will not sell in the market, instead selling to MS/GS at daily VWAP proportionate to market purchases.
  • Morgan Stanley Europe SE and Goldman Sachs Bank Europe SE engaged to execute in sequential portions as riskless principal.
  • Maximum 300m ordinary shares, representing ~6.5% of issued share capital as of 15 May 2026.
  • Purchases on both London Stock Exchange and Spanish Stock Exchanges.
  • Per-session cap: no more than 25% of 20-day ADV.
  • Price cap: lower of (i) higher of last independent trade/highest current bid, and (ii) 105% of 5-day average market value.
  • Shares held in treasury pending cancellation, subject to AGM approval of related capital reduction.

body:
• Ingredion confirmed a non-binding indicative all-cash offer at 595p per share for Tate & Lyle.
  • Maximum headline value of 615p per share / ~GBP2.74 billion based on 445.4m shares in issue, per Tate & Lyle's earlier statement responding to press speculation.
  • Tate & Lyle shareholders would retain the right to a final FY (March year-end) dividend of up to 13p and an interim dividend of up to 7p for the six months to September, subject to board and shareholder approval.
  • Offer "follows a number of earlier approaches from Ingredion to the board"; discussions ongoing but no certainty of a firm offer.
  • Ingredion has a PUSU deadline of 11 June to declare a firm intention.
  • Ingredion reserves the right to "introduce other forms of consideration and/or vary the mix or composition of consideration of any offer" — leaves door open to non-cash elements.
  • Strategic rationale per Ingredion: "Ingredion believes a potential transaction would deliver significant benefits to customers, consumers, employees and Ingredion shareholders."
  • Shares closed up ~45% at 542p (market cap ~GBP2.42bn), still trading at a notable discount to the 595p indicative level — reflecting deal/antitrust uncertainty given Ingredion is a direct US starches & sweeteners peer.

• Announced a new global multi-year partnership with ServiceNow to embed Experian's Ascend capabilities directly into ServiceNow's AI Platform workflows.
  • Partnership targets agentic AI scaling, with initial use cases in employee onboarding, third-party risk management (including fraud and identity verification), and model life cycle/risk governance.
  • Positioning rationale: cites industry research that data limitations are the primary barrier for 8 in 10 organisations adopting agentic AI — partnership aims to move clients beyond pilot deployments.
  • Experian Ascend Platform will be natively connected to ServiceNow AI Platform, allowing AI agents to access Experian's decisioning data within existing enterprise workflows.
  • Keith Little, President - Experian Software Solutions: *"This partnership cements Experian's position as a global leader in AI innovation, giving organisations the foundations to deploy agentic services with confidence."*
  • Cathy Mauzaize, President EMEA at ServiceNow: *"Businesses are ready to move beyond experimentation, and this partnership gives them exactly what they need to scale."*
  • No financial terms, revenue contribution, or guidance impact disclosed; strategically extends Experian Software Solutions' reach into new industries and regulated enterprise workflows beyond core financial services.

body:
• Full-year 2026 EPS guidance reiterated at up to 21 cent; trading in line with expectations.
  • Closed and forward order book at €1.5bn (Homebuilding + Partnerships), up from €1.3bn on 10 March (+15%).
  • Homebuilding units sold, signed or reserved: 1,828, up from 1,252 on 10 March (+46%).
  • Five additional Homebuilding sites launched plus seven further phases selling across existing developments.
  • Partnerships order book ~€800m, underpinning average annual gross profit contribution of at least €60m.
  • On track to deliver ~2,750 units in 2026, including ~1,600 Homebuilding units.
  • ~€45m of land sales planned in 2026 as part of portfolio optimisation toward larger-scale sites.
  • Homebuilding gross margin expected in excess of 21%, with efficiency gains offsetting build cost inflation despite Middle East conflict macro impact.
  • H2-weighted delivery profile reiterated, supporting strong H2 cash generation and further shareholder returns.
  • Refinancing completed: total committed funding raised to €550m from €450m.
  • New 5-year €450m RCF with AIB, Bank of Ireland, Barclays, HBFI, and new lender ING.
  • Issued €100m of 7-year private placement notes to MetLife, broadening lender base with long-dated institutional capital.
  • Share buyback increased by a further €25m to €50m total; ~€25m already returned under the January 2026 programme.
  • Cumulative shareholder returns since 2021 will reach ~€465m on completion of current programme.
  • Innovation: external wall façade system on track at NUA's Carlow facility; integrated solar PV and battery storage driving demand.
  • Board: Conor Murtagh replaces Stephen Garvey as Executive member of the Environmental and Social Responsibility Committee from conclusion of 2026 AGM.
  • 2026 Interim Results scheduled for 10 September 2026.
  • CEO Stephen Garvey: "We have made a strong start to 2026, building on the momentum from the second half of last year… the business is on track to deliver its full year guidance, with the outlook for the years ahead remaining positive."
  • CEO on funding: "The addition of ING to the banking syndicate and the €100m issuance to MetLife is extremely positive and will assist us in further driving the delivery of much needed homes in Ireland."

• Sky News reports BT has revived talks over a sale or partnership of its international operations (formerly BT Global), nearly a year after pausing earlier negotiations.
  • Potential counterparties named: AT&T, Orange and Verizon.

  • Total payments to governments of $23.84bn across extractive activities in 2025.

  • US taxes were a net -$23.9m refund (IRS -$25.2m), offset by $1.12bn royalties to ONRR (Gulf of America Central $1.05bn).
  • India recorded a net tax refund of -$14.6m (BG Exploration & Production India).
  • Mexico payments were negative -$0.14m; small materiality items.
  • Large in-kind (barrel) settlements notable in Norway ($2.12bn / 30,514 KBOE at Ormen Lange), Nigeria ($1.24bn to NNPC / 22,346 KBOE), Malaysia (multiple, totalling >$1.6bn in-kind), Oman ($518m at gov. selling price), and Brazil ($459.7m / 7,627 KBOE via Pré-Sal Petróleo).
  • Brazil Libra/Mero project bonuses of $285.8m and BM-S-9/11/Atapu fees of $1.38bn point to continued pre-salt licence/lease cost intensity.
  • Qatar Pearl GTL alone generated $2.91bn in payments to QatarEnergy.
  • Oman Block 6 Concession taxes of $3.39bn — single largest project-level tax line in the report.
  • Materiality threshold £86,000 per payment type; joint-control entity payments excluded (so Pearl-style consolidated entities included, but JV-only flows not captured).

  • Cash: adjusted operating cash flow $36.2m (cash conversion 85% vs 84%); adjusted free cash flow $26.5m (+86.6%).
  • Leverage: adjusted net debt $152.0m, down from $174.0m at FY25 (down $22.0m / ~12.6%); leverage 1.8x (FY25: 2.2x). Board to consider capital allocation “towards the end of the year” as leverage approaches ~1.5x.
  • Group KPI framework simplified: Items sold (replaces lots sold/listed, web sessions), updated GMV and take rate definitions (now include Chairish/Real Estate/ESN/white label); THV, conversion rate, lots listed, web sessions, bids placed no longer reported.
  • Trading KPIs (pro forma): items sold 3.6m (+2%); GMV $1.8bn (flat) with A&A GMV +5% to $0.5bn and I&C GMV -2% to $1.3bn; take rate 7.1% (HY25: 6.6%, +0.5ppt).
  • A&A: pro forma take rate 17.7% (+1ppt); LiveAuctioneers improvements delivered +8.2% GMV and +9.4% items sold on that platform.
  • atgShip: mandate coverage expanded to >80% of GMV (from 20% at end of H1 FY25); first-time winning bidders using atgShip show 20% higher repeat purchase rate vs non-users; ~1,400 auction houses onboarded (vs ~1,000 at FY25).
  • Chairish: H1 revenue growth described as “good”; profitable in the first half; operational synergies track $8m run-rate in FY27, with $6m to be delivered in FY26 and $3m realised in H1.
  • I&C: softer H1 attributed to agricultural headwinds, white-label adoption, and auction house consolidation; agricultural GMV down 27%; Proxibid re-platforming: first auction house in testing; rollout targeted during FY27.
  • Additional cost programme launched in March: $4m run-rate savings expected in FY27, with modest H2 FY26 benefit; exceptional cost noted (e.g., $2m in H1 for reorganisation/cost review).
  • FY26 guidance upgraded: Group revenue growth 5–6% (constant currency, pro forma incl. Chairish) vs prior 4–5%; adjusted EBITDA margin 34.5–35.5%; “Group leverage well below 2x by end FY26”; strong free cash flow maintained.
  • Management: Duncan Painter appointed CEO 5 May 2026; quote: “For FY26, having delivered a positive start to the year driven by A&A momentum, we are pleased to modestly upgrade our guidance. We expect another period of strong free cash flow generation.”
  • Capital structure / equity: share premium cancellation approved (special resolution 22 Jan 2026), court-confirmed 3 Mar 2026 and registered 13 Mar 2026, reclassifying £236.8m from share premium to retained earnings.

• BP has acquired a 40% participating interest in a production sharing contract in Uzbekistan, buying 20% from each of SOCAR and Uzbekneftegaz, who each retain 30%.
  • PSA covers six blocks in the North Ustyurt region: Boyterak, Terengquduq, Birqori, Kharoy, Qoraqalpoq and Qulboy.

  • Operations are in first phase, with SOCAR conducting seismic activities (early-stage exploration, no near-term production impact).
  • Gio Cristofoli, BP's regional president for Azerbaijan, Georgia and Turkiye: "We believe Uzbekistan has significant resource potential and see this as an opportunity to support the exploration and development of the country's oil and gas resources, delivering long‑term benefits to the region."
  • Uzbekistan Energy Minister Jurabek Mirzamahmudov called it "not merely a commercial agreement, but a direct testament to international investors' confidence in the reforms being carried out in Uzbekistan and in our strategic course toward the development of the energy sector".
  • SOCAR President Rovshan Najaf framed the deal as deepening Azerbaijan-Uzbekistan energy cooperation.
  • Context: Bloomberg reported earlier this month BP is considering exiting UK North Sea operations, potentially fetching ~GBP2 billion in a full divestment.
  • BP is targeting around USD20 billion in divestments by end-2027, signalling continued portfolio rotation toward lower-cost international upstream barrels.
  • Shares rose 0.5% to 550.50p on Wednesday morning; Brent at USD106.12/bbl vs USD108.07 prior late session.

body:
• Non-binding all-share offer agreed with Schroder Real Estate Investment Trust (SREIT) to acquire Picton Property Income.
  • Terms: Picton holders receive 0.190 LondonMetric shares + 0.881 SREIT shares per Picton share.
  • Implied value: ~£403.4m, or 78.2p/share based on offerors' Monday close.
  • Premium: 7.0% to Picton's 73.1p undisturbed price, but a 5.6% discount to Picton's December portfolio value (NAV).
  • Split of acquisition: LondonMetric 46% / SREIT 54% of Picton.
  • Post-deal, Picton shareholders to own 4.0% of enlarged LondonMetric and 48.2% of enlarged SREIT.
  • LondonMetric's existing 11.1% stake in SREIT dilutes to 5.8%; agreed 6-month lock-up post-completion on remaining SREIT stake.
  • Schroders agreed to a 10bp reduction in SREIT management fee across all tiers.
  • Picton board "minded to unanimously recommend" if firm offer made.
  • Letter of intent to vote in favour received from TR Property Investment Trust (~11.4% of Picton).
  • Sector weightings of both acquirers' portfolios expected to be broadly unchanged post-allocation of Picton assets.
  • SREIT LTV expected to fall into its 25–35% target range post-deal.
  • Both acquirers expect the deal to be earnings accretive, with "a very material, immediate increase in dividend income for Picton's shareholders".
  • Consortium statement: offer "retains Picton's good quality portfolio in the UK-listed arena and... provides Picton shareholders with the opportunity to crystallise a premium to the share price at the undisturbed date whilst reinvesting into two enlarged, UK-listed REITs that will enjoy the various benefits of enhanced scale".
  • Background: follows Picton's January strategic review considering "a merger with other UK REITs"; LondonMetric/SREIT consortium shortlisted in March.
  • Share reaction on day: Picton -1.1% to 72.30p; SREIT -2.8% to 46.95p; LondonMetric -1.9% to 184.10p.
  • No certainty a firm offer will be made.

Demonstrating a clinically meaningful improvement in lung function in a population with significant unmet need highlights the potential of ETD001. For IP Group, this represents another example of our model providing investors with access to differentiated deep science opportunities."

body:
• Portfolio company Enterprise Therapeutics reported positive Phase 2 results for ETD001, its lead inhaled candidate for cystic fibrosis.
  • Trial met its primary efficacy outcome in the 10% of CF patients with the highest unmet medical need.
  • Demonstrated a clinically meaningful improvement in lung function over 28 days vs placebo.
  • Safety profile: overall well-tolerated, adverse events consistent with expectations for the population.
  • Next steps: advance ETD001 into longer-duration Phase 2b studies, in combination with CFTR modulator therapies, and into other muco-obstructive lung diseases.
  • CEO Greg Smith: "This is a highly encouraging clinical milestone for Enterprise Therapeutics and a strong validation of its differentiated approach to cystic fibrosis. Demonstrating a clinically meaningful improvement in lung function in a population with significant unmet need highlights the potential of ETD001. For IP Group, this represents another example of our model providing investors with access to differentiated deep science opportunities."
  • Note: non-regulatory release; no financial impact, valuation uplift or stake size disclosed.

body:
• Net revenues RMB315.7bn, +4.9% YoY; net product revenues +1.0%, net service revenues +20.6%.
  • Segment revenue mix: JD Retail +1.8%, JD Logistics +29.0%, New Businesses +9.1%.
  • Category mix: Electronics & home appliances -8.4%; General merchandise +14.9%; Marketplace & marketing +18.8%; Logistics & other services +21.7%.
  • GAAP net income attributable to shareholders RMB5.1bn vs RMB10.9bn (-53%); non-GAAP net income RMB7.4bn vs RMB12.8bn (-42%).
  • Diluted EPS per ADS RMB3.54 vs RMB7.19; non-GAAP diluted EPS per ADS RMB5.12 vs RMB8.41.
  • Operating income RMB3.8bn vs RMB10.5bn; operating margin 1.2% vs 3.5%; non-GAAP operating margin 1.8% vs 3.9%.
  • JD Retail operating margin hit record 5.6% (vs 4.9%); operating income RMB15.0bn vs RMB12.8bn.
  • New Businesses operating loss widened sharply to RMB10.4bn (margin -164.9% vs -23.1%) on JD Food Delivery investment; management notes sequential narrowing of losses.
  • JD Logistics operating income RMB1.0bn vs RMB0.1bn; margin 1.7% vs 0.3%.
  • Cost pressures: Fulfillment +18.5% (7.4% of revenue vs 6.6%); Marketing +45.8% (4.9% vs 3.5%) on new business promotion; R&D +48.6%; G&A +48.7%, partly due to RMB635m SAMR fine related to third-party cake-shop food safety compliance failures.
  • Non-GAAP EBITDA RMB8.0bn vs RMB13.7bn; margin 2.5% vs 4.6%.
  • Free cash flow -RMB6.5bn (vs -RMB21.6bn Q1 2025); TTM FCF RMB21.6bn vs RMB37.6bn a year ago.
  • Cash, restricted cash and short-term investments RMB215.7bn (US$31.3bn), down from RMB225.4bn at year-end 2025.
  • Buyback: repurchased ~1.6% of shares outstanding for US$631m in Q1; US$1.4bn remaining under US$5.0bn programme through Aug 2027; annual dividend paid in April.
  • Inventory turnover days lengthened to 38.3 (TTM) vs 32.8 a year ago.
  • Founder award: boards of JD Health, JD Logistics, JD Industrials and JD Property each approved granting Richard Liu RSUs equal to ~2% of each subsidiary's share capital, 4-year vesting.
  • Strategic moves: launched Joybuy online retail in Europe (UK, Germany, Netherlands, France, Belgium, Luxembourg) on 16 March; JoyExpress "Double 11" (211) delivery now covers 30+ European cities/40m people.
  • 7Fresh Kitchen expanded to Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Shenzhen and Tianjin; JD Food Delivery unit economics improving sequentially.
  • Segment reclassification: from Jan 2026, JD Logistics on-demand delivery shifted to serving third-party merchants directly, reducing internal revenues and New Businesses external on-demand revenues.
  • JD Ecosystem headcount >900,000; trailing 12-month personnel expenditure RMB166.4bn.
  • CEO Sandy Xu: "Our user base and shopping frequency continued to expand robustly, with annual active customers hitting a new record... JD Retail demonstrated remarkable resilience throughout the quarter, with profitability reaching record levels... we remain confident in our full-year trajectory and long-term value creation."
  • CFO Ian Su Shan: performance "anchored by the steady progress of JD Retail, as general merchandise categories and high-margin businesses including marketplace and marketing revenues continued to outperform, alongside a substantial narrowing of sequential losses in our New Businesses, led by JD Food Delivery."

• Announced pricing terms of cash tender offer for any and all of its $500m outstanding 3.125% Senior Notes due Nov. 2, 2026.
  • Purchase Price set at $995.83 per $1,000 principal, based on 4.125% UST due Oct 31, 2026 reference yield of 3.786% plus fixed spread of 25bps.
  • Holders also receive accrued and unpaid interest up to (but excluding) the settlement date.
  • Tender Offer expires 5 p.m. NYC time, 12 May 2026; expected settlement 15 May 2026.
  • Tender is conditioned on completion of a contemporaneous New Notes Offering of senior debt securities, whose proceeds will fund the repurchase — effectively a refinancing of the 2026 maturity ahead of its November maturity date.
  • No minimum tender condition; offer may be amended, extended or terminated.
  • Any Notes not tendered are expected to be repaid at maturity, with the Company planning to deposit funds with Deutsche Bank National Trust Company (trustee) to satisfy and discharge the indenture shortly after settlement.
  • J.P. Morgan Securities LLC acting as exclusive Dealer Manager; D.F. King & Co. as tender/information agent.

body:
• Top end of FY26 guidance achieved: Adjusted EBITDAaL €11.6bn and Adjusted FCF €2.6bn on guidance basis.
  • Total revenue +8.0% to €40.5bn (FY25: €37.4bn), boosted by Three UK consolidation, partly offset by FX.
  • Service revenue +8.8% reported to €33.5bn; organic +5.4%, growth in all segments except Germany.
  • Adjusted EBITDAaL +3.8% reported to €11.4bn; organic +4.5%.
  • Group Adjusted EBITDAaL margin 28.1% (FY25: 29.2%), down 1.1pps reported.
  • Operating profit swung to €2.8bn from a €0.4bn loss (no FY26 impairments vs €4.5bn prior-year charge).
  • Adjusted basic EPS 10.72c vs 7.87c (+36%); basic loss per share narrowed to 1.20c from 15.86c.
  • Adjusted FCF €2.6bn (FY25: €2.5bn, +2.9%); Free cash flow €1.8bn (-3.0%).
  • Net debt rose to €25.4bn (FY25: €22.4bn) due to VodafoneThree consolidation and €2bn buyback; targeting lower half of 2.25-2.75x leverage range.
  • Liquidity: €12.4bn cash + short-term investments (down from €16.3bn); €7.6bn undrawn RCF.
  • Final dividend 2.3625c; total FY26 DPS 4.6125c, +2.5% YoY (progressive policy from Nov 2025).
  • Second €2bn buyback completed 11 May 2026; total capital returned in FY26 €3.1bn; €9bn returned over three years.
  • FY27 guidance: Adjusted EBITDAaL €11.9–12.2bn; Adjusted FCF €2.6–2.9bn; Europe Adj. EBITDAaL €7.6–7.9bn.
  • FY27 restructuring/integration costs to peak at ~€0.7bn (incl. ~€0.4bn VodafoneThree integration).
  • Safaricom consolidation would add pro-forma ~€1.5bn to Adj. EBITDAaL (subject to Kenya High Court ruling 18 May 2026).
  • Germany: organic service revenue -0.2% FY26 but improved to +1.3% in Q4 (vs -0.2% Q3 reported figure; Q4 organic 1.3%); EBITDAaL organic -3.3%, margin 35.0% (-1.0pp). Broadband ARPU on new customers +30% YoY in Q4.
  • Germany broadband base -202k; mobile contract base -103k; competitive intensity and MDU TV transition (-0.8pp) cited.
  • UK: organic service revenue +0.3%; Adj. EBITDAaL organic +4.5%; reported revenue +30% on Three consolidation; margin 20.5% reported (organic +1.4pp).
  • UK Business organic service revenue -4.5% on planned managed services contract terminations.
  • VodafoneThree: agreed buyout of CKHGT's 49% stake for £4.3bn (€4.9bn) cash via share cancellation (announced 5 May 2026); confirms £700m annual cost & capex synergies by FY30; network sharing across 10,000 sites ahead of plan.
  • Other Europe: organic service revenue +0.5%; Adj. EBITDAaL organic +3.7%; margin +1.5pp organic; Portugal weak on 4th-operator entry.
  • Türkiye: organic service revenue +45.2% (ex-hyperinflation +10.8%); Adj. EBITDAaL organic +47.6%; 100MHz 5G spectrum acquired for $627m; 5G launched April 2026.
  • Africa: organic service revenue +12.9%; Adj. EBITDAaL organic +14.0%; margin 33.9% (+0.6pp).
  • M&A: Vodacom to acquire 20% of Safaricom for €1.81bn total (15% from Kenya govt €1.36bn, 5% from Vodafone €0.45bn); pending Kenya High Court ruling 18 May 2026.
  • VodafoneZiggo sale to Liberty Global agreed: €1.0bn cash + 10% stake in new Ziggo Group entity; expected close H2 2026.
  • Skaylink acquired Dec 2025 for €175m (cloud/digital); Telekom Romania Mobile acquired Oct 2025 for €30m.
  • Vantage Towers: Vodafone's share hit by €464m non-cash impairment of INWIT investment.
  • Vodafone Idea CLAM indemnity settled 31 Dec 2025 via €219m cash payments (offset by VIL service charges) and assignment of 3,280m VIL shares; €256m liability recognised.
  • UK class action (Gutmann loyalty penalty): claim values now £557m (Vodafone) and £197m (Three) post strike-out; defences filed Feb 2026; trial-setting hearing 1-2 July 2026.
  • Adjusted ETR 28.1% (FY25: 25.3%); reported ETR 96.8% inflated by €358m UK DTA derecognition and €305m German DTA write-down.
  • Pre-tax ROCE (controlled) 6.6% (-0.4pp); post-tax ROCE stable at 4.4%.
  • Capital intensity 18%; medium-term ambition reiterated for double-digit organic Adj. FCF growth.
  • CEO Margherita Della Valle: "After the transformation of the last three years, we are now a simpler company with a stronger growth outlook."
  • CEO: "We returned to top line growth in Germany, alongside strong performances across Africa and in Türkiye."
  • CEO: "We are now well set for mid-term growth."
  • Board/Exec changes: Pilar López appointed Group CFO 1 Dec 2025 (succeeding Luka Mucic); Simon Segars new SID; Anne-Françoise Nesmes joined as NED; Guillaume Boutin appointed CEO Vodafone Investments & Strategy May 2025.

  • H1 FY27 scheduled capacity ~51 million seats, +28% YoY.
  • H1 FY27 forward bookings 44% sold, +2ppt YoY.

  • Management has strategically used promotional fares to stimulate H1 FY27 demand and protect load factors amid geopolitical uncertainty.
  • CEO Jozsef Varadi: "we have proactively pivoted the affected capacity to our core markets and are seeing strong demand trends through the peak summer period across our network."
  • CEO on positioning: "Wizz Air's financial strength, including cash liquidity, hedge positions and our highly fuel-efficient fleet, continues to underpin our ability to grow our business with structural competitive advantages."
  • CEO reiterated focus on strengthening leadership in the faster growing CEE region.
  • FY25 reference: 63.4 million passengers carried.
