body:
• Rule 2.4 announcement: LondonMetric and Schroder Real Estate Investment Trust ("SREIT") have reached agreement in principle on key financial terms of a non-binding, indicative all-share consortium offer for Picton Property Income.
  • Proposed consideration: 0.190 LondonMetric shares + 0.881 SREIT shares per Picton share.
  • Implied value: 78.2p per Picton share, valuing Picton equity at £403.4m (LondonMetric 46% / SREIT 54%, matching split of Picton's GAV).
  • Premium of ~7.0% to Picton's 11 May close (73.1p); only ~0.9% to the 77.5p Undisturbed Date price (12 Jan 2026, pre-formal sale process); ~13.0% to 1-month VWAPs prior to Undisturbed Date.
  • Implied EPRA NTA discount of ~9.2% and ~5.6% discount to Picton's 31 Dec 2025 portfolio valuation (£699.1m).
  • Post-completion: Picton holders would own ~4.0% of enlarged LondonMetric and ~48.2% of enlarged SREIT; LondonMetric's existing 11.1% SREIT stake would dilute to ~5.8%.
  • Permitted dividends: Picton can pay 0.95p quarterly dividend for period to 31 Mar 2026 plus future ordinary dividends only to extent covered by cash earnings; excess would trigger consideration reduction.
  • Strategic rationale: addresses Picton's sub-scale listed challenges (per its 13 Jan 2026 formal sale process), keeps assets in UK-listed REITs, strengthens SREIT's LTV into 25–35% target range and inherits below-market cost of debt.
  • Expected to be earnings accretive for both LondonMetric and SREIT, with a "very material, immediate increase in dividend income" for Picton shareholders (not a profit forecast).
  • SREIT fee changes: Schroders to cut SREIT management fee by 10bps across all tiers (new tiers: 0.8% up to £500m NAV/mcap, 0.7% £500m–£1bn, 0.6% above £1bn) plus a 1-year IMA fee waiver spread over 24 months on Picton NAV inherited by SREIT; in exchange SREIT moves to a 3-year fixed IMA, then 1-year notice.
  • LondonMetric agrees to a 6-month lock-up on its residual SREIT stake post-completion.
  • Enlarged SREIT to continue to be led by Fund Managers Nick Montgomery and Bradley Biggins; talent review of Picton staff to follow.
  • Picton Board would be minded to unanimously recommend a firm offer on these terms, subject to reciprocal due diligence, finalised terms and documentation.
  • Shareholder support: letter of intent from TR Property Investment Trust covering its 11.4% Picton stake (58.43m shares) to vote in favour.
  • Pre-conditions to firm offer: confirmatory DD, Picton lender consents, final LondonMetric/SREIT board approvals, and confirmation of Picton board recommendation.
  • Likely structure: Guernsey scheme of arrangement (contractual offer reserved as alternative); Panel dispensation means Consortium not bound by Rule 2.6(a) 28-day PUSU while in Picton's formal sale process.

body:
• FY26 guidance reinstated: Adjusted PBT expected in range of £18m–£25m (previously withdrawn at March AGM update due to Middle East conflict).
  • Record H1 booking volumes of 324k, +7% YoY, vs total ATOL market +3%; travelled volumes +22% to 201.6k.
  • Booked TTV £626.2m, +2% (+£14.5m).
  • Revenue £52.2m, down £7.2m (-12%); includes £0.7m exceptional cancellations from Middle East conflict.
  • Adjusted revenue £52.9m (-£6.4m); ABV down 4% on mix shift to Cities, shorter lead times and switch from UAE/Eastern Med to Western Med.
  • Adjusted EBITDA £6.4m vs £12.8m (-50%); margin collapsed to 12.1% from 21.6%.
  • Adjusted PBT £2.3m vs £8.4m; statutory PBT loss of £3.2m vs £4.5m profit.
  • Marketing costs down £4.5m YoY; marketing as % of revenue improved to 41% from 44%.
  • Overheads up £3.1m to £21.6m on annualisation of FY25 tech investments; restructuring cut headcount by 108, delivering c.£4m annualised savings.
  • Exceptional items £2.6m (vs £0.9m): £0.7m Middle East cancellations, £1.5m restructuring, balance legal/share repurchase costs.
  • Net debt £27.5m (improved £2.0m YoY); £88m of facility headroom; £209.9m in customer trust account (-£14.3m YoY).
  • RCF drawn £27m (vs £40m prior year) under £120m facility (+£30m accordion) expiring Sept 2029; covenants not breached.
  • Interim dividend maintained at 1.0p; FY payout policy 25% of PAT, so total FY26 dividend expected lower than prior year.
  • Capital returns: c.£33m committed in H1 (£29.1m share buybacks + £4.2m dividends); 10.2m shares repurchased/cancelled for £22m, plus £3m cancelled from Sept 2025 purchases.
  • Current trading: bookings +9% over last 6 weeks since H1 end as Summer approaches; activity "stabilised to a more consistent trading pattern".
  • Strategic KPIs: App MAUs +29%; app booking mix 38%; in-year repeat bookings +24%; 2-year repeat rates +17%; funnel conversion +24%.
  • Strategic expansion areas: City volumes +116% (Krakow, Amsterdam); Republic of Ireland +74%; Cruise test-and-learn launched.
  • AI: app launched on ChatGPT (24 March) as first mover in UK package space; Anthropic integration in progress; LLM share of voice 15% in Q2, ranked 3rd in UK AI-driven holiday discovery.
  • Automation: 98% of bookings automated (vs 60% in FY22); recently eliminated manual fulfilment of c.130,000 bookings/year.
  • Lead time shift: bookings with <90 day lead time +23%; Winter 26 bookings +20%; higher-value Summer/Eastbound bookings deferred ("wait and see").
  • Operational drag from conflict: rolling UAE cancellations, elevated customer contact, increased flight schedule changes.
  • CEO Shaun Morton: "we have today reinstated guidance and the Board is confident in delivering FY26 Adjusted PBT in the range of £18m to £25m" and "I am confident that On the Beach is well placed to satisfy this demand and deliver a solid Summer trading performance."
  • Addressable market now stated at over 50m passengers following Cities, Cruise and Ireland expansion.

• System-wide revenue $1,166m, +9% YoY; Group revenue $958m, +4% YoY.
  • 2026 guidance maintained: adjusted EBITDA $585m–$625m, Company-owned revenue growth of at least 4% (flat costs), recurring managed fee income $80m, investment grade credit rating commitment.
  • Signings accelerated to 382 in Q1 2026 (vs 224 in Q1 2025, +71%); openings 222 (vs 165, +35%).
  • Managed & Franchised fee income $39m, +70% YoY; recurring management fee revenue $16m, +80% YoY; system (partner) revenue +41% YoY to $260m.
  • M&F rooms open 336,000 (+48%), centres open 2,082 (+53%), pipeline 231,000 rooms — implies potential annual system revenue >$1.9bn when mature.
  • M&F RevPAR: Managed -5% to $164 (drag from immature new openings; ex-2025 openings $222); Franchised & JV +1% to $492.
  • Company-owned: revenue $906m, +2% YoY (return to growth); RevPAR +6% to $389; only 5 new locations signed, 9 opened; capex in line with prior guidance.
  • IWG Network blended RevPAR -2% to $348 (ex-2025 openings $378).
  • Net financial debt rose to $858m (from $715m at YE25 and $721m at Q1 25), driven by $53m share buyback (19.5m shares), annual bonus payments, and a temporary working capital drag from automated invoicing rollout shortening payment days.
  • Net debt expected to normalise through 2026 but end 2026 slightly above YE25 levels.
  • $75m returned to shareholders YTD 2026; $100m of buybacks announced for 2026; >$230m returned since December 2023 Investor Day.
  • Most of the 0.5% Convertible Bond put back to the Company in December 2025; full-year interest cost on €300m 5.125% 2032 bond now hitting 2026; first refinancing not until 2030; all bonds fixed-coupon, hedged into USD.
  • Management taking proactive cost reduction actions in Q2 and beyond to address inflationary pressures from conflicts and macro uncertainty.
  • CEO Mark Dixon: "I am delighted with our strong start to 2026 as we continue the rapid growth of our network supported by increasing sales despite the challenging economic backdrop."
  • Dixon on demand drivers: "Potential customers are requiring more flexibility in their Real Estate strategy to address the uncertainty arising from the impact of conflicts and the growing influence of AI. This is resulting in record levels of Enterprise customer enquiries."
  • Dixon on capital model: "Signings and openings continue to grow, allowing the flywheel of our business model to deliver greater cashflow while requiring less capital to grow than historically."
  • Q1 2025 comparatives now restated under US GAAP (from IFRS) following H1 2025 basis change.
  • Next update: Interim results 11 August 2026; AGM 19 May 2026; final 2025 dividend paid 29 May 2026.

• Group revenue +3.5% to £589.0m (HY25: £569.3m); organic growth of 2.2%, expected to accelerate in H2.
  • Adjusted operating profit +4.4% to £33.4m; adjusted operating margin 5.7% (+10bps).
  • Profit before tax +8.6% to £25.5m; adjusted EPS +9.6% to 30.9p.
  • Interim dividend raised +4.9% to 7.0p (HY25: 6.7p), payable 8 July 2026.
  • Record order book of £945m (HY25: £908m), underpinning FY26 confidence.
  • Balance sheet swing to pre-IFRS16 net cash of £10.6m (HY25: net debt £11.8m).
  • Exceptional/amortisation charge £6.6m (HY25: £5.9m); reported operating profit £26.9m (+3.0%).
  • Discontinued operations loss of £0.9m driven by an increased Allenbuild provision following internal reassessment of contractual claim settlement costs.
  • Rail: subdued renewals as Network Rail prioritises reactive maintenance; delivered record emergency response volumes; remains Network Rail's largest infrastructure services supplier; CP7 (£45.4bn, £31.9bn renewals) runs to March 2029.
  • Highways: RIS3 confirms £27bn over five years with renewals nearly doubling to £8.4bn (vs RIS2 £4.8bn); interim one-year £4.8bn cycle included +18% maintenance/renewals spend (~£1.3bn); SDF1 frameworks extended 5 months to February 2028.
  • Water: record activity levels; working 10 of 12 largest combined regions, 8 in line/ahead; AMP8 commits £104bn investment (£45bn new infrastructure vs AMP7's £11bn); Thames Water work unaffected by client's financial position.
  • Renewables: French subsidiary of Full Circle undergoing restructuring review following underperformance flagged in April trading update; 63 new MSAs signed, total 747 turbines under contract.
  • T&D: RIIO-T3 final determination approved £28.1bn; sits within ~£90bn pipeline to 2031; Emerald Power trading in line with pre-acquisition expectations.
  • Nuclear: Sellafield performance impacted by ongoing site-wide industrial action; underpinned by UK's ~£4bn annual decommissioning programme.
  • M&A activity: Emerald Power acquired Oct 2025 for up to £11.3m (initial £6.8m, £4.5m deferred remuneration); EDS acquired 30 April 2026 for up to £13m (initial £10m); PWR-X acquired 7/11 May 2026 for £1.1m total (£0.75m initial). EDS described as "immediately earnings enhancing".
  • Five-year track record: organic revenue +40%, total revenue +80%, adjusted EPS +63%, 7 acquisitions deploying £135.4m, average ROCE 27%, free cash conversion 63.4%.
  • CEO Paul Scott: "With a record order book afforded to us by highly visible, committed, long-term spending cycles, we remain confident in continuing on this growth trajectory and we look forward to delivering against our full year expectations."
  • Outlook: confident in delivering FY26 expectations; active M&A pipeline supported by strong balance sheet.

• IAG announced the final results of its reverse bookbuilding invitation to repurchase its outstanding EUR 825m 1.125% Senior Unsecured Convertible Bonds due 2028.
  • EUR 819m in aggregate principal (99.3% of outstanding) was validly tendered and accepted for purchase.
  • Initial Repurchase Price set at EUR 138,950 per EUR 100,000 principal, to be adjusted via a reference delta of 99% based on the two-day VWAP of IAG shares from 11 May 2026 versus the 8 May 2026 closing price.
  • Final Repurchase Price expected to be announced 12 May 2026 after market close; accrued interest of EUR 3.06 per EUR 100,000 principal payable.
  • Settlement expected on or around 19 May 2026, subject to the Financing Condition; tendered bonds will then be surrendered for cancellation.
  • Only EUR 6m principal will remain outstanding post-settlement — below the 15% threshold — triggering IAG's intention to exercise the clean-up call to redeem the residual stub at par plus accrued interest.
  • BofA Securities and HSBC Continental Europe acted as Joint Dealer Managers.
  • Announcement made by Nicholas Cadbury, CFO & Chief Sustainability Officer.
  • Context: removes potential equity dilution overhang from the 2028 convertibles (issued 2021 during pandemic-era liquidity raise) and simplifies IAG's capital structure, consistent with the group's ongoing balance sheet deleveraging following its return to investment-grade metrics.

• Launched a consent solicitation on its £750,009,000 Fixed Rate Reset AT1 Perpetual Subordinated Contingent Convertible Securities callable 2029 (ISIN: XS1043552261).
  • Purpose: align the subordination provisions of these Securities with the "Recent AT1 Subordination Provisions" already embedded in all of Lloyds' other AT1 issuances expected to be outstanding at 1 July 2026.
  • These are the last remaining Lloyds AT1s without the updated subordination language, following the 30 April 2026 notice to redeem the $500m 6.75% AT1s callable June 2026.
  • If passed, Lloyds intends to reclassify the Existing Preference Shares as Tier 2 Capital from 1 July 2026, increasing Group Tier 2 Capital by c.£400m.
  • Existing Preference Shares affected: 9.25% (GB00B3KS9W93), 6.413% (USG5533WAA56/US539439AC38), 6.657% (US539439AE93/US539439AF68), 9.75% (GB00B3KSB238).
  • Background: the prefs ceased to count as Tier 1 at end of CRR transition (31 Dec 2021); previously left ranking pari passu with AT1 to avoid infection risk to legacy AT1s — now being remediated in line with the PRA's Nov 2020 "Dear CFO" letter and BoE resolution planning objectives.
  • PRA has provided confirmation of no objection to the Proposal.
  • Rating agencies (Fitch, Moody's, S&P) have been provided the draft memorandum; no rating change expected on the Securities.
  • Consent fees: 0.25% Early Consent Fee (deadline 4:00pm London, 22 May 2026); 0.10% Late Consent Fee (by Expiration Deadline 10:00am, 29 May 2026); equivalent fees available to Ineligible Securityholders for valid abstentions.
  • Meeting: 2 June 2026, 10:00am at Clifford Chance LLP, London.
  • Management signal on optionality: "in the event the Extraordinary Resolution does not pass, the classification of the Existing Preference Shares is one of the factors that the Issuer will consider alongside the review of any potential optional redemption of the Securities at a future date" — implying a possible call of the 2029 AT1s if consent fails.

body:
• Revenue +18.3% to US$66.43m (Q1 2025: US$56.18m), driven by realised gold price of US$4,816/oz (+66.3%) offsetting lower volumes.
  • Gold production at Blanket 14,767 oz (-20.9%); consolidated gold sales 13,784 oz (-28.9%); 3,656 oz bullion on hand at quarter-end.
  • FY2026 Blanket production guidance reiterated at 72,000–76,500 oz, weighted to H2.
  • Production miss driven by constrained access to higher-grade areas: head grade fell from 3.1 g/t to 2.5 g/t (-19.4%), recovery down to 91.9% (from 93.6%); tonnes milled flat.
  • Central Shaft contributed only 56% of milled tonnage vs planned 65%; stockpile (2.0 g/t) filled gap but diluted grade.
  • Assay grades improving month-on-month: ~2.55 g/t Dec 2025 → 3.02 g/t Mar 2026 → ~2.86 g/t April 2026.
  • On-mine cost US$1,740/oz (+44.8%); AISC US$2,765/oz (+53.9%) — both inflated by lower volumes/fixed cost absorption, not absolute cost creep (on-mine US$ total +3.0%, AISC US$ total +9.4%).
  • Gross profit +19.2% to US$32.10m; EBITDA +50.2% to US$33.87m; PAT +69.4% to US$18.91m; Basic EPS +77.8% to US$0.80.
  • Net cash from operations +41.5% to US$18.87m; free cash flow US$12.28m vs US$4.86m (+152.6%).
  • Capex US$5.28m (-8.4%), all at Blanket.
  • Quarterly dividend maintained at 14 US cents/share, payable 5 June 2026.
  • Liquidity transformed: total US$191.1m (cash US$170.0m, bullion US$16.4m), reflecting January 2026 issuance of US$150m convertible senior notes due 2033 (5.875% coupon, conversion price ~US$40.51, 25% premium); capped call options purchased for US$14.44m (cap ~US$56.72).
  • Net fair value gain on derivatives of US$4.00m in the quarter (Q1 2025: US$1.59m loss).
  • Mitigation actions underway: contractor appointed to accelerate development; shift system moving from 6 to 7 days/week; ~36kt stockpile buffer being built ahead of Central Shaft winder upgrade later in 2026; additional ball mill commissioning mid-2026 to lift throughput from 97.55 to 101.98 tph.
  • Bilboes financing progressing: peak funding US$484m; FS (Nov 2025) shows 10.8-year LOM, 150koz/yr avg production, AISC US$1,061/oz, post-tax NPV8% US$582m, IRR 32.5% at US$2,548/oz (significantly better at spot); both interim facility and project finance facility discussions advanced.
  • Deep-level drilling (10,312m completed Mar–Dec 2025) confirms continuity of Blanket, Eroica and Lima orebodies at depth, including new BLK7 orebody; updated resource/reserve statement expected during 2026.
  • Motapa: US$3.8m allocated for 2026; maiden sulphide MRE at Motapa North targeted for 2026.
  • Safety: LTIFR improved to 0.0 (Q1 2025: 2.4); TIFR 2.2 (-54.3%).
  • Diesel only ~3% of operating costs and ~2% of power (vs 8% in 2020); solar covers ~20% of power; exports routed via South Africa — no impact from Middle East geopolitics.
  • CEO Mark Learmonth: "We continue to trade in line with market expectations and with a strong gold price environment, improving operational performance at Blanket and continued progress towards developing Bilboes, we remain confident in our strategy and our ability to deliver long‑term value for shareholders."

body:
• Q1 operating profit EUR351m, +77% YoY (vs EUR198m), well ahead of analyst expectations.
  • Revenue EUR7.18bn, +1.9% YoY (vs EUR7.04bn).
  • Net debt fell sharply to EUR4.18bn from EUR5.95bn.
  • Guidance cut: FY2026 profit and free cash flow will be lower than previously anticipated due to Middle East-driven fuel cost surge.
  • FY2026 fuel cost now expected at ~EUR9bn (incl. hedging & sustainability), +27% vs EUR7.08bn in 2025, above prior February guidance of EUR7.0–7.4bn.
  • Capacity growth target lowered from 3% — now ~1% in Q2 and ~2% in Q3; winter schedules under review.
  • ~70% hedged for remainder of year; expects to recover ~60% of higher fuel costs via pricing, capacity redeployment, and cost controls.
  • Only ~3% of capacity had Gulf exposure pre-conflict; redeployed to Bangkok, Singapore where Middle Eastern carriers have cut flights.
  • Q2 booked revenue resilient at 80%, in line with historical levels.
  • Premium cabin demand strong; North & South Atlantic routes (~half of group capacity) remain robust; business travel revenue growing.
  • Softer demand flagged in Eastern Mediterranean; short-haul European market competitive.
  • Margin/profit improvements across all airlines except Aer Lingus, which faces long-haul pricing pressure (per Panmure Liberum).
  • EUR1.5bn buyback continues; remaining EUR1bn to run through February 2027.

Time Period Fiscal Q2 2026 (three months ended 31 March 2026)

  • Massive Q2 beat:

Net income was $9.2 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2026 and diluted EPS were $0.16, compared to net income of $4.2 million and diluted EPS of $0.08 in the same quarter last year

;

adjusted EPS of $0.18 topped the consensus estimate of ($0.05) by $0.23

.

$769.2 million, an increase of 34.5% compared to $571.7 million a year earlier

, well above the ~$678–691m consensus.

11% organic increase and a 24% contribution from acquisitions

.

Gross profit was $98.9 million vs $71.4 million a year earlier

;

G&A was $63.6m (8.3% of revenue) vs $46.7m (8.2%) prior year

.

$93.3 million, maintaining an approximately 12.1% margin on significantly higher revenue

(+35% YoY).

about 80% to 85% of the next 12 months of contract revenue is covered by backlog

.

  • FY2026 guidance raised to:

revenue $3.59–$3.65 billion, net income $159.0–$162.0 million, Adjusted net income $170.4–$174.2 million, Adjusted EBITDA $552.0–$564.0 million with a 15.38–15.45% Adjusted EBITDA margin

;

organic growth still expected at about 7% to 8% for fiscal 2026

.

.

  • M&A cadence:

Four Star Paving was the 4th acquisition in FY26 and 17th since FY24; expects to fund Four Star from Q3 cash flow without new long-term debt

.

$77 million of cash on hand and $150 million of availability under its credit facility

;

operating cash flow reached $65.2 million for the quarter, up from $55.6 million a year earlier

.

debt running at 3.23 times trailing 12-month EBITDA versus a target near 2.5 times

.

more than half of liquid asphalt needs now supplied internally; over 80% of revenue is covered by a liquid asphalt index, complemented by physical diesel hedging and terminal storage of roughly two to two and a half months of inventory

eight data center projects in Texas totaling ~$100m of contract value, 12 Nashville warehouse projects totalling ~$28m, FIFA World Cup-related work in Houston, North Carolina road widening tied to the U.S. Open at Pinehurst in 2029, and a taxiway reconstruction at Eglin Air Force Base

.

management is engaged with Congress on surface transportation reauthorization, with both parties working toward a bill in the $500–$600 billion range; that level was not assumed in the Road 2030 plan, which instead assumes normal mid-single-digit annual increases

targets doubling the size of the company, generating $1 billion of annual EBITDA and expanding EBITDA margins to about 17%

"We are pleased with our team's strong execution this quarter as we continue to advance CPI's proven growth strategy. Our differentiated business model, built on cost pass-through, vertical integration, and a decentralized partnership approach, remains a powerful and often underappreciated driver of sustainable results."

"With the peak construction season ahead in the second half of our fiscal year, we are raising our FY 2026 outlook, and we are well-positioned to execute against this record backlog and sustain our growth momentum."

shares up roughly 5% in pre-market following the release, adding to a strong run of ~6.2% over the past week and over 11.6% in the last month

.

body:
• Pretax profit fell 12% to £629m (FY25: £715m); basic EPS down 9.2% to 8.63p.
  • Revenue up 11% to £12.66bn (+12% constant currency).
  • Organic sales growth of 2.1% in a "muted" market.
  • Profit decline driven by higher operating costs and increased interest on lease liabilities.
  • Free cash flow up 36% to £462m (FY25: £339m).
  • Final dividend raised to 0.87p (from 0.67p); full-year dividend up 20% to 1.20p.
  • Launching rolling annual £200m share buyback; first £100m tranche to complete in H1 FY27.
  • Q1 FY27 trading: organic sales flat, like-for-like down 2.3%.
  • LFL by region: Europe -4.2%, UK -4.0%, North America -0.6% (+0.4% ex-Finish Line conversion), Asia Pacific +5.2%.
  • FY27 PBT (pre-adjusting items) guidance widened to £750m–£850m vs £852m in FY26 (FY26 itself -7.7% YoY on this measure).
  • FY27 free cash flow guided to £460m–£520m.
  • CEO Régis Schultz: "We delivered a resilient performance, achieving organic sales growth of 2.1% despite tough market conditions," citing "customer‑led focus, alongside disciplined cost and capital management".
  • Schultz on outlook: "Whilst we continue to expect muted market growth in FY27, we remain confident in JD Group's medium‑term trajectory, underpinned by our strong brand partnerships and agile, multi‑brand model."
  • Shares +5.8% to 71.94p in early trade, top FTSE 100 gainer.

body:
• Reaffirmed ambition to grow adjusted earnings by 50% by 2030, citing greater portion of portfolio subject to rent reviews in 2026/2027 and development pipeline.
  • GBP5.9m incremental annual rental income added YTD from lease events covering 12% of portfolio, with a 13% absolute uplift in rent across these events.
  • Lease events on Blackstone-acquired assets delivered stronger uplifts: UKCM logistics +15% and urban assets +24%.
  • Guides to higher like-for-like rental growth in 2026 as asset management opportunities accelerate.
  • New Newark letting secures GBP3.3m annual rent; new Cambridge pre-let secures GBP1.6m; both expected to deliver yield on cost >7%.
  • Around GBP7m of annual rental income in solicitors' hands.
  • Data centres: first site at Manor Farm, Heathrow (107MW) "primed for launch"; planning decision expected from Secretary of State on or before 9 June; would recognise strong development profits in 2026 subject to planning and securing a pre-let.
  • Planning decision expected near-term on second data centre site in Chelmsford.
  • LTV reduction underway from 33.2% (Dec) supported by capital rotation.
  • >GBP270m of disposals/exchanges completed as at 30 April, majority a logistics portfolio sold above valuation; 93% of non-strategic UKCM assets sold, exchanged or under offer.
  • CEO Colin Godfrey: entered 2026 with "strong operational momentum" and continues "to make excellent progress across each of our three growth drivers."
  • CEO on reversion capture: "We are capturing rental reversion and driving income growth across our high-quality portfolio through our active and hands-on approach, particularly within the assets acquired from Blackstone."
  • CEO on macro/geopolitics: "Occupier demand for UK logistics remains healthy, supporting positive engagement and leasing activity across both our investment and development portfolios. To date, we have not seen any impact from the conflict in the Middle East but continue to monitor the situation closely."
  • CEO on outlook: "Looking ahead, with a greater proportion of the portfolio subject to rent reviews in 2026 and 2027 and substantial development opportunities within logistics and data centres, we are well placed to accelerate income growth. Consequently, we remain confident in our ambition to grow adjusted earnings by 50% by 2030."
  • Shares +0.7% at 154.18p on the day.

body:
• GMV $389.9m, +6% YoY (vs $367.4m).
  • Revenue $120.7m, +4% YoY (vs $116.4m); split: Purchase $77.9m (flat), Consignment & fees $42.9m (+11%).

  • Adjusted EBITDA growth outpaced net income due to higher tax expense (provision $3.15m vs $0.66m) from reduced stock-based comp tax benefits.
  • Cash & investments $204.0m, zero financial debt (cash $195.3m + ST investments $8.7m); up from $185.8m at FY25 year-end.
  • Operating cash flow H1 FY26 $29.0m vs $9.5m prior year (boosted by $17.8m payables-to-sellers swing).
  • Consignment = 81% of consolidated GMV.
  • Segment GMV: GovDeals +5% (held back by winter weather disruption and lower real estate activity); RSCG +10% (consignment-led, D2C channel growth, purchase GMV ~flat); CAG +3% (heavy equipment strength, industrial lumpy).
  • Segment revenue: GovDeals +11% (higher take rates from service expansion + lower real estate mix), RSCG +1% (but direct profit +29%, margin 26% vs 20%), CAG +12%, Machinio & Software +12%.
  • Registered buyers 6.3m, +8% YoY; completed transactions ~280k, +9%; auction participants ~985k (flat).
  • Q3 FY26 Guidance: GMV $425–465m; GAAP Net Income $7.0–10.0m; Adjusted EBITDA $17.0–20.0m; GAAP Diluted EPS $0.21–0.30; Adjusted Diluted EPS $0.30–0.39.
  • Q3 expected to be seasonally strongest quarter; consignment GMV expected at low-to-mid 80% of total; revenue/GMV mid-to-high 20s; segment direct profit/revenue mid-to-high 40s.
  • Q3 RSCG purchase GMV expected sequentially flat with less favourable product mix; CAG: continued heavy equipment growth and strong energy project pipeline.
  • FY26 effective tax rate guided 30–34%, Q3 in mid-30s; cash taxes rising in FY26 as US federal NOL carryforward fully utilised in FY25.
  • Buyback: $15.0m remaining authorisation; $1.5m repurchased H1 FY26.
  • Diluted share count expected ~33.0m.
  • CEO Bill Angrick: "Our broad industry coverage, robust buyer liquidity and operating leverage drove a strong second quarter with expanded profitability."
  • Angrick on strategy: "we are building a more scalable and attractive marketplace business which will create long-term value for both customers and shareholders."

  • Broking: spot business, revenue and profits materially ahead YoY, supported by geo-political complexity, robust trading flows, extended voyage distances, elevated chartering rates and asset prices.

  • Management framing: "The trend of increased global trade dislocation and complexity which we have seen over the last decade has continued."
  • Reiterates positioning for further M&A opportunities; trading environment "continues to support growth."
  • Context: Clarksons has delivered 23 consecutive years of dividend growth; FTSE 250, ~2,250 staff across 70+ offices.

body:
• Shares down 1.7% to 3,156p as rejigged distribution policy and mixed Q2 outlook offset earnings beat.
  • Adjusted earnings rose 24% to USD6.92bn (Q1 2025: USD5.58bn), beating consensus of USD6.36bn.
  • Adjusted EBITDA up 16% to USD17.74bn (vs USD15.25bn), beating USD16.73bn consensus.
  • Drivers: higher oil prices, higher refining margins, lower opex, higher Lubricants margins; partly offset by lower volumes.
  • Citi noted adjusted net income was 10% above consensus, but consensus had already moved 15% higher post-April trading statement.
  • Downstream led the beat (refining margin capture and oil trading); Upstream held back by lag effects in pricing formulas missing March price rally.
  • CEO Wael Sawan: results were "strong" in a quarter marked by "unprecedented" disruption in global energy markets.
  • Cash flow from operations fell to USD6.06bn (from USD9.28bn); free cash flow down to USD2.93bn (from USD5.32bn).
  • Working capital outflows of USD11.2bn mainly from commodity price impact on inventory and receivables.
  • Basic EPS USD1.01 (vs USD0.79); adjusted EPS USD1.22 (vs USD0.92).
  • Net debt up 27% to USD52.61bn (from USD41.52bn YoY).
  • Distribution policy rebalanced: dividend hiked 9.1% YoY to USD0.3906/share (+5.0% QoQ), vs prior ~4% annual growth target.
  • Quarterly buyback cut to USD3bn from USD3.5bn; first reallocation since 2023; to be completed by Q2 results.
  • 40%–50% CFFO payout policy firmly reiterated; total cash yield ~9% if USD3bn/qtr buyback sustained.
  • 2026 capex guided to USD24–26bn (including ARC Resources), raised from prior USD20bn guidance at FY25 results.
  • 2027–2028 capex outlook unchanged at USD20–22bn.
  • Q2 integrated gas production guided 580–640 kboe/d, well below Visible Alpha consensus of 874 kboe/d.
  • Q2 LNG liquefaction volumes guided 6.8–7.4mt vs 7.9mt consensus.
  • Shortfall reflects Middle East conflict (Qatar) and higher planned maintenance.
  • Pearl facility (Qatar) damage repair expected to take around one year.
  • Australian LNG site also hit by temporary cyclone-related stoppages.
  • AJ Bell's Dan Coatsworth: "it wasn't all plain sailing" given Qatar facility damage and Australia LNG disruption.
  • Jefferies' Wilson saw "logic" to the rebalancing, noting shares up >30% YoY but ~0.5% lower 2026 distribution yield.
  • Citi's Syme said the buyback/dividend rebalance "should have been made several quarters ago".
  • Hargreaves Lansdown's Nathan: ARC acquisition helps diversify supply post-Qatar, but markets cautious as buyback pace slowed with net debt up 27%.
  • Brent traded at USD98.59/bbl on the day vs ~USD102 prior close.

body:
• Aberdeen Investments to become alternative investment manager of Herald Investment Trust, bringing ~GBP1.6 billion AUM (incl. Herald Worldwide Technology Fund) under its management.
  • Herald's outgoing lead manager Katie Potts plus seven HIML colleagues expected to transfer to Aberdeen.
  • Herald proposes tender offer for up to 66% of issued shares at close to NAV.
  • Saba Capital (~30% holder, Herald's largest shareholder) has given irrevocable undertaking to tender its shares.
  • Three-year standstill agreement signed with Saba: activist commits to not voting against the Herald board's recommendations at any GM.
  • Broader Aberdeen-Saba deal: up to eight further Aberdeen investment trusts with ~GBP12.5 billion combined AUM can opt into similar standstill arrangements at the discretion of their independent boards — a notable defensive perimeter against further activism.
  • CEO Jason Windsor: "Completion of this transaction will further grow our franchise and demonstrates our innovation and commitment to the sector."
  • AIC CEO Richard Stone called it a "creative solution" and "successful outcome for shareholders."
  • Saba framed it as a "major liquidity win" and "landmark outcome," noting Herald is the sixth of seven trusts from its December 2024 campaign to yield a material liquidity/governance result.
  • Boaz Weinstein (Saba): "This is what shareholder engagement looks like when boards act in the interests of the people they serve, and it is what Saba will keep demanding across the UK investment trust sector."
  • Market reaction: Aberdeen shares +1.8% to 218.20p; Herald +2.4% to 3,030.33p.

FY27 Guidance:

  • PBTAI £750m-£850m (wider-than-internal range due to uncertainty; FY26: £852m).
  • FCF £460m-£520m (FY26: £462m).
  • Gross capex ~£400m (FY26: £401m); net new space contribution +2-3% (FY26: +4.2%).

CEO Régis Schultz quote: "We delivered a resilient performance, achieving organic sales growth of 2.1% despite tough market conditions… This customer-led focus, alongside disciplined cost and capital management, supported a 36% increase in free cash flow."

  • Brendan Nelson stood down from HSBC UK board on 29 April 2026; will leave Group Technology & Operations Committee post-AGM and Group Audit/Risk Committees post-Interim Results.

  • Strong start with first 5 weeks +11.8%; growth slowed in H2 of the quarter on Middle East conflict disruption and tougher comps (last year boosted by unusually warm UK weather).
  • FY pretax profit guidance raised to £1.22bn from £1.21bn (+£8m), vs £1.19bn delivered in the 52 weeks to 31 Jan 2026; £28m additional sales drop-through.
  • FY full price sales growth guidance lifted to +5.0% from +4.5% (UK +2.8%, International +14.4%).
  • Q2 guidance: full price sales +4.0% (UK +1.0%, International +17.0%).
  • UK sales +4.4% (vs 1.3% guided): Online +10.1%, Retail -3.4%.
  • International sales +12.8%, well short of ~20% buy-side hopes due to Middle East service disruption; exit rate accelerated to +18.3%.
  • Middle East crisis cost now estimated at £47m vs prior £15m, mainly higher transport/fuel costs.
  • Mitigation: overseas price increases of "no more" than 8% to be implemented in May; UK extra costs offset by cost savings and margin gains, no price rises beyond the 0.6% already planned.
  • Guidance assumes fuel costs and supply chain disruption remain at current levels.
  • Jefferies (Frederick Wild): "This upgrade, we believe unexpected by the market, is complemented by a complete offset to Middle East cost increases (more pricing/cost saves offsetting the pressure emerging locally) and no signs of change to underlying consumer behaviour."
  • JPMorgan (Georgina Johanan): "This is a solid statement from Next, although we think it could be seen as slightly disappointing in the context of elevated expectations heading into the print, where some data points had suggested an ongoing acceleration"; views update as "somewhat reassuring" for broader UK retail.
  • UBS raised FY27 PBT forecast by 1% to £1.23bn; views 5.0% sales guidance as "conservative", sticks with 6.0%.
  • AJ Bell (Russ Mould): called Next a "well-oiled machine"; "Such is Next's skill at managing expectations that even when confronted with an event as disruptive as the conflict in the Middle East it still feels able to lift guidance."
  • Peel Hunt described update as "better-than-feared".
  • Hargreaves Lansdown (Aarin Chiekrie) flagged tough Q2 UK comps from last year's warm weather and M&S cyber disruption: "While some caution is wise, Next has developed a track record of under-promising and over-delivering in recent years. And as a leader in the UK market, it's better placed than many UK retail peers to navigate a tougher backdrop".

body:
• Response to Ryanair CEO Michael O'Leary's proposed two-drink limit at airport hospitality venues; Wetherspoon disagrees with the proposal.
  • Describes the suggestion as difficult to manage and a "big brother" approach; argues airport venues are already highly supervised with CCTV, experienced managers, and police/airport authority oversight.
  • Participates in the industry "One Too Many" campaign to discourage anti-social behaviour on flights.
  • Airport sales mix over last six months: 65% from food, soft drinks, tea and coffee; only 35% alcoholic, with a significant proportion served alongside meals.
  • Drinks breakdown: tea/coffee 17% of overall drink sales; soft drinks 23%.
  • Operating history cited: Heathrow since 1992, Gatwick since 1994, Stansted since 2003 — states it has never been told its customers caused issues on flights.
  • Management view: a two-drink limit would push consumption to unsupervised "off-trade" purchases (off-licences/supermarkets) before passengers reach the airport.
  • Company (and O'Leary) believe the problem is worse on incoming flights from certain destinations where controls are weaker.
  • Chairman Tim Martin: "A two-drink limit would be extraordinarily difficult to implement, short of breathalysing passengers, and would, in our opinion, be an overreaction- especially since many of the problems stem from incoming flights."
  • No financial guidance, trading update, or KPI changes disclosed — statement is reputational/policy-related only.

  • UK Consumer: NTS +6% to £4.14bn; Revenue -2% to £204m due to commission rate cut from 5.0% to 4.5% (Apr 2025); ex-cut, revenue would have grown 7%. Adj EBITDA -2% to £87m.
  • International Consumer: NTS +3% CCY to £1.10bn; Revenue +10% CCY to £60m; adj EBITDA loss narrowed from -£20m to -£11m. South-East France NTS +26% post Trenitalia expansion (Paris-Marseille avg fares -27%); Spain rebalanced toward profitability; Germany/RoE -6%.
  • Trainline Solutions: NTS +14% to £1.08bn (fastest unit); B2B Distribution +36%, International B2B +58%; revenue +4% to £189m; adj EBITDA +11% to £101m. Lost Cross-Country white-label; ScotRail white-label loss expected in FY27.
  • Buyback: £94m repurchased of current £150m programme as at 30 April 2026; £294m total since Sept 2023 (23% of issued share capital); 60.1m shares cancelled in FY26 at avg £2.52.
  • Net debt £170m (1.0x adj EBITDA), up from £76m (0.5x) - reflecting £147m of buybacks plus £82.7m convertible bond redeemed Jan 2026.
  • New £450m RCF signed July 2025, extended to £600m in Feb 2026, maturity July 2028 with two 1-yr extension options to 2030; covenants unchanged (net debt/EBITDA ≤3.0x; EBITDA/finance charges ≥4.0x); £221.8m undrawn.

  • Regulatory win: UK Government confirmed (March 2026) that once GBR is established, Delay Repay will be claimable from third-party retailers including Trainline - described as customers' "number one ask".

  • France: April 2026 French Senate amendment would oblige SNCF Connect to distribute competitor tickets on FRAND terms (early stage).
  • AI: launched Travel Forecast (3m+ users updated), AI Travel Assistant (2m+ conversations), Delay Repay notifications (1m redirected); Trainline app integrated into ChatGPT (March 2026); #1 cited rail app in Google AI Search across all core markets and ChatGPT (ex-France); GenAI delivers c.3% of new International foreign-travel customers.
  • KPIs: 27m active customers globally; 18m UK; digital railcard users +16% to 2.7m; 45% share of 16-30 railcard users; double-digit % growth in hotel and insurance ancillaries.
  • Effective tax rate 30% (FY25: 28%), elevated by deferred tax asset reduction on share-based payments (lower share price).

• Total saleable Cu production +28.7% YoY to 2,177t (9m FY2025: 1,691t), excluding stockpiled fine concentrate at Roan and stockpiled Molefe ore.
  • Roan production +112.7% to 1,999t Cu units, including 779t in oxide concentrate fines (new stream commenced August 2025).
  • Sable Refinery cathode output 957t (+27.4% vs 751t).
  • Q3 production softer at 634t vs Q1 939t, reflecting commissioning delays and seasonal rains.
  • FY2026 copper production guidance under review due to: (1) updated Molefe mine plan with accelerated stripping to merge Pits 2 & 3, completion expected July 2026; (2) delay in commissioning/ramp-up of expanded Roan dewatering circuit, which deferred the additional ~110t equivalent Cu units step-up.
  • Updated guidance to be issued "within the coming weeks" once consultant confirms Molefe progress and dewatering circuit reaches steady state.
  • Expanded Roan Cu concentrate dewatering facility currently at ~75% of targeted 110–120tpm contained Cu; ramp-up underway during May 2026.
  • Dewatering circuit design capacity ~230tpm contained Cu, enabling simultaneous processing of the 14,000t historical fine concentrate stockpile (~2.7% Cu) plus ongoing 110–120tpm fine concentrate.
  • Roan concentrator running at ~30,000tpm; front-end upgrade offers potential >40,000tpm post seasonal rains and dewatering ramp-up.
  • Roan annual maintenance shutdown 8 May 2026 for 6 days; Sable to keep operating by drawing down in-process stocks.
  • Molefe Mine: 250,162t of Cu reef ore mined in the period; 20,064t dispatched to Sable at average 1.84% Cu grade; on-site stockpile now exceeds 2.3Mt.
  • Molefe pre-stripping: >250,000t removed in April 2026 alone; post-integration mine expected to ramp from ~12,000t/quarter to >30,000t/quarter of Cu reef ore at expected ~1.4% total Cu grade pre-sorting.
  • JORC-compliant resource competent person's report expected Q4 CY2026, subject to assay turnaround; further drill campaigns to be considered thereafter.
  • Molefe Mine investor presentation planned for June 2026.
  • LTIFR 0.00 for the period (FY2025: 1.40).
  • SA Head Office relocating to Irene, Centurion in early June 2026 — right-sizing after disposal of SA chrome/PGM operations.
  • Group target reiterated: 25,000tpa copper production via the three-pillar strategy (Roan concentrator, Sable refinery, regional mining + Large Waste Rock Project).
  • CEO Leon Coetzer: "We continue to make strong progress in delivering our Zambia copper strategy, with Roan sustaining targeted production rates and the expanded concentrate circuit now entering ramp-up after minor technical and logistical delays, marking a key step-change in our processing capability."
  • CEO on Molefe: "While heavy rains impacted the quarter, momentum remains strong as we advance the mine plan and plan increased production."
  • CEO on outlook: "This integrated approach gives us strong confidence in delivering sustained and scalable growth in copper production."

body:
Barclays PLC

Publish Date 1 May 2026

-

Barclays Bank Delaware (operating as "Barclays US Consumer Bank") has completed the acquisition of Best Egg, Inc., a US direct-to-consumer personal loan origination platform

, originally announced on 28 October 2025.

  • Deal value: $800 million (per Cleary Gottlieb and Delaware Business Now), based on

tangible net assets of $275 million

, with

consideration representing a high-single digit Price/Earnings multiple

on 2026 earnings.

-

Expected to consume approximately 16bps of Group CET1 capital upon Completion. The Transaction will not affect Barclays' stated total distribution target of at least £10 billion between 2024 and 2026

— no impact on shareholder distribution target.

  • Best Egg scale:

facilitated over $40 billion in personal loans to more than two million customers since 2013; in 2025, expected to facilitate more than $7 billion in personal loan originations via its platform

;

currently services approximately $11 billion in personal loans

.

  • Capital-light model retained:

Barclays expects to continue this model and retain a small portion of Best Egg's new lending flow on its balance sheet

; loans funded via securitisation programmes and forward flow arrangements with alternative asset managers.

-

The acquisition, including the realisation of synergies, is expected to generate an attractive return on investment for Barclays, comparable to our three highest-returning UK businesses, over time

.

-

The acquired business will continue to operate under the "Best Egg" brand and be managed by Barclays US Consumer Bank

;

Best Egg is headquartered in Wilmington, Delaware and employs approximately 500 employees

.

  • Strategic rationale:

Best Egg adds a scaled, proven, and capital-light personal lending platform that complements the US Consumer Bank's partnership-driven credit card and deposit businesses

.

  • CEO C.S. Venkatakrishnan:

"The U.S. is a strategically important growth market for Barclays. The Best Egg acquisition strengthens our US Consumer Bank with a proven, capital-light personal lending platform. It supports greater diversification, capital efficiency, and attractive returns over time, while enhancing our ability to serve customers across the U.S. consumer finance market."

  • USCB CEO Denny Nealon:

"We're excited to welcome Best Egg's customers and colleagues to Barclays. This acquisition aligns with our strategy by expanding our personal lending capabilities and supporting the development of a more diversified, digitally-focused consumer bank. Best Egg brings a proven platform and a talented team, and we look forward to building on those strengths together."

We remain confident in achieving the targets we set out in February 2026."

  • Exit linked to Carnival's December announcement to collapse the Carnival Corp & PLC dual-listing structure into a single entity, Carnival Corp Ltd, trading solely on the NYSE.
  • Company rationale (verbatim): "Unification will eliminate the different pricing between the two share listings, simplify governance, reporting and administrative complexity, and is expected to increase our company's weighting in key US stock indices and reduce costs – together strengthening our ability to deliver long-term shareholder value while preserving our core business strategy and key shareholder voting and economic rights."
  • Carnival share price 1,956.48p, +51% over 12 months.
  • XP Power share price 1,750.00p, more than doubled from 697.00p over 12 months.

We have recently seen some softening in footfall and reservations, and limited increases in the cost of some materials."
  • Prothero added caution extends to land investment decisions into FY27, citing planning and site viability challenges.

body:
• Income guidance upgraded: now expects FY26 income excluding notable items at the top end of the previously guided £17.2–17.6bn range; all other FY25 guidance reaffirmed (excludes forthcoming Evelyn Partners acquisition).
  • Total income £4,358m, +9.5% YoY, +0.8% QoQ; income excluding notable items £4,223m, +6.9% YoY, -1.1% QoQ (impacted by two fewer days, tax-related deposit outflows, lower mortgage margins).
  • Operating profit £2,033m, +12.2% YoY; attributable profit £1,432m; EPS 17.9p, +15.5% YoY.
  • RoTE 18.2% (Q1'25: 18.5%; Q4'25: 18.3%).
  • NIM 2.47%, +20bps YoY, +2bps QoQ — driven by deposit margin expansion from strong hedge income.
  • Cost:income ratio (ex-litigation/conduct) 46.5%, improved 2.1ppt YoY; >£100m of additional cost savings generated in Q1.
  • Other operating expenses £2,027m, +4.8% YoY (transformation, pay award, investment), -8.3% QoQ (seasonal Q4 drop-off).
  • Impairment charge £283m (26bps loan impairment rate), vs £189m Q1'25 and £136m Q4'25; includes c.£140m multiple economic scenario (MES) update reflecting weaker outlook from Middle East conflict.
  • ECL provision rose to £3.7bn; coverage 0.84%; PMAs of £0.3bn retained; unsecured Stage 3 flows up due to seasoning of post-2022 credit card growth.
  • CET1 ratio 14.3%, +30bps QoQ (Q1'25: 13.8%); 65bps capital generation pre-distributions in the quarter; £2.2bn of RWA management benefits.
  • RWAs £196.0bn, +£2.7bn QoQ (franchise growth, market/counterparty risk; partly offset by RWA actions).
  • TNAV/share 400p, +16p QoQ, +53p YoY.
  • Net loans (ex-central items) +£7.2bn QoQ to £396.4bn: Retail mortgages +£3.3bn; C&I +£3.8bn (Corporate & Institutions led).
  • Customer deposits (ex-central items) +£3.1bn to £444.8bn; C&I +£5.1bn offset by seasonal tax outflows in Retail and PB&WM.
  • AUMA -£1.8bn QoQ to £56.7bn (negative markets -£1.7bn, gilt redemptions for tax); AUM net inflows £0.9bn, c.23,000 new-to-invest clients (>50% uplift).
  • LCR 144% (-3ppt QoQ); loan:deposit ratio (ex-repos) 89%, +1ppt QoQ.
  • Segment RoEs: Retail Banking 24.6%, PB&WM 21.1%, Commercial & Institutional 18.3%.
  • Retail Banking impairment £184m (vs £114m Q4) — non-repeat of mortgage securitisation benefit, MES update, Stage 3 credit card flows.
  • C&I impairment £94m (vs £19m Q4) on MES update.
  • New partnerships announced: Rightmove (digital mortgage distribution) and Sainsbury's Group (cards, loans, savings); NatWest Boxed reclassified into Retail Banking from Q1'26.
  • Onboarded 24,000 new startups in C&I, +25% YoY; >£1.1bn social housing committed (on track for £10bn by 2028).
  • Capital actions: $0.8bn 5.908% Tier 2 issued March 2026; €0.8bn senior unsecured (2037) issued Feb 2026; redeemed $1.0bn and £0.5bn senior notes.
  • Buyback: 51m shares repurchased/cancelled YTD for £313.7m; further 10.7m shares cancelled post-period for £63.5m.
  • Foreseeable ordinary dividend accrual £2,553m; foreseeable charges £608m (relates to buybacks).
  • Macro assumptions revised: base case inflation peak >3.5%, GDP growth slowing to 0.4%, unemployment peak 5.7%, BoE rate paused; extreme downside weight raised to 14.2% (from 13.1%) reflecting stagflation risk.
  • New litigation disclosed: NWMSI named in Oracle bond offering class action (Sept 2025 issue); plaintiffs allege offering documents misleading regarding AI-related debt plans; Oracle has indemnified underwriters.
  • Swaps antitrust litigation: defendants filed summary judgment motion in March 2026.
  • US fixed-income monitorship paused May 2025 and deemed no longer necessary; probation extended to December 2026.
  • CEO Paul Thwaite: "NatWest Group's strong performance in the first quarter of 2026 reflects our consistent delivery for customers and shareholders."
  • CEO on macro: customers need support to "navigate increasing uncertainty and to achieve their goals."

• Net sales $2.73bn, +8.0% reported but -2.6% on constant days/FX basis vs prior year.
  • Net earnings $117m; EPS $1.90 vs $1.15 prior year (+65%); adjusted EPS $1.90 vs $1.52 (+25%).
  • Adjusted operating margin 5.5% vs 4.8%; adjusted gross margin 24.8% vs 24.1%.
  • Prior-year comp benefited from system conversion impact and had four fewer days.
  • Q2 2026 adjusted EPS guidance: $2.50–$2.60, excluding restructuring/one-time charges (one less shipping day in Q2).
  • Repurchased 607,000 shares for $64m during the quarter.
  • Net debt $1.24bn; net debt/adjusted EBITDA 0.9x; cash $872m.
  • Free cash flow $7.8m vs -$85.4m prior year; capex $102m vs $89m.
  • Segment performance (reported / adj. constant days & FX):
  • Global Ceramic: sales +10.4% / -0.2%; adj. operating margin 5.0% vs 4.8%.
  • Flooring NA: sales +2.0% / -4.1%; adj. operating margin 4.0% vs 3.0%.
  • Flooring ROW: sales +12.2% / -4.4%; adj. operating margin 9.8% vs 9.1%.
  • Middle East conflict (intensified end-February) flagged as key new headwind: rising energy/oil/gas derivative costs hitting raw materials; price increases being implemented across many categories and geographies, with further increases possible.
  • Cost impact skewed to H2: "The impact of higher cost raw materials will be greater in the second half of the year due to our flow through of inventory."
  • Pricing/cost lag: "We will not see the full impact of our pricing actions and rising input costs until the third quarter."
  • Demand commentary: commercial channel solid across regions; residential remodeling and new home construction soft as consumers defer purchases on economic uncertainty; higher-end products outperforming.
  • Order backlog continues to grow one month into Q2.
  • Tax: Q1 included a one-time $30.7m benefit from US legal entity restructuring and Brazilian tax credits (prior-year items).
  • Management actions: containing costs, reengineering products, limiting capital expenditures, executing prior restructuring projects.
  • CEO Lorberbaum: "Our performance was in line with our expectations despite a challenging environment."
  • Long-term view: "deferred remodeling of the aging housing stock across our regions will significantly increase flooring demand" as cyclical rebound approaches.

• Pretax profit fell 19% to £298m (vs £368m prior year) on flat revenue of £2.92bn.
  • Adjusted pretax profit flat at £483m; adjusted basic EPS up 7.1% to 208.5p (vs 194.6p).

  • Premier Inn UK accommodation sales and RevPAR both +1% YoY, with return to market growth from Q2.
  • UK Food & Beverage sales down 8%; Premier Inn Germany sales up 13%.
  • Profitability hit by high cost inflation and interest costs.
  • Shares fell 6.7% to 2,225p on the day.
  • New five-year plan targeting "material step up in margins and returns" by FY2031.
  • Plan extends the Accelerating Growth Plan: replaces all remaining branded restaurants (Beefeater, Bar + Block, Brewers Fayre), reduced UK/Germany capex, higher cost savings, freehold disposals.
  • 3,800 UK & Ireland job cuts out of ~30,000 workforce (~13%).
  • FY2027 impact: AGP extension to reduce F&B sales by £140–160m and profits by £40m; net £10m profit reduction after offsetting original AGP gains.
  • By FY2031 targets: +£275m incremental adjusted pretax profit, net capex cut by £1bn, £1.5bn freehold property sales to fund growth capex, ROCE +500bps, and £2bn free cash flow available for shareholder returns.
  • Hotel room target: 96,000 rooms by FY2031 (vs ~86,600 currently); long-term aspiration of 125,000 rooms.
  • CEO Dominic Paul: "In light of significant cost increases in the form of business rates and national insurance, as well as the implied market discount to our inherent value, we've looked hard at the options open to us to maximise value creation over the medium and long-term."
  • CEO on model: the "right one" but "we can improve our approach."
  • CEO on capital strategy: "We will refocus our capital spend and recycle more of our freehold real estate, driving increased margins and returns, reducing our capital intensity and increasing cash returns for shareholders."
  • Forward booked position ahead of last year with "positive trading momentum."
  • Flagged "limited visibility of short-term market demand and inflation," citing Middle East crisis.

body:
• 2026 production guidance reaffirmed across all major commodities.
  • Marketing division full-year adjusted EBIT seen "comfortably exceeding" the top end of the USD2.3bn–USD3.5bn long-term guidance range, supported by Q1 performance and energy marketing activities supplying fuel to mining assets.
  • CEO Gary Nagle on Middle East conflict impact: "Although the impact of the conflict on our industrial business was limited in the first quarter, recent and emerging impacts are now manifesting, primarily as an increase in input costs, most notably diesel and acid consumption, and the generally weaker USD."
  • Cost pressures expected to be "more than offset" by stronger commodity prices widening margins.
  • Q1 own-sourced production deltas YoY:
  • Copper +19% to 199,600t
  • Silver +15% to 4.9m oz
  • Chrome ore +3% to 830,000t
  • Cobalt −39% to 5,800t — due to DRC export quota system introduced late 2025, applying until at least end-2027; KCC and Mutanda have sufficient inventory to fill quotas near-term; normalisation expected over next year.
  • Nickel −9% to 17,200t — Sudbury furnace disruption
  • Zinc −17% to 176,900t; Lead −17% to 41,200t — end of mine life at Loretta (late 2025) and lower Kazzinc contribution
  • Gold −53% to 68,000 oz
  • Steelmaking coal −22% to 6.5mt
  • Energy coal −2% to 22.9mt
  • 2026 production guidance vs 2025 actuals:
  • Copper: 810–870kt (vs 851.6kt) — implies flat-to-slightly-down midpoint
  • Zinc: 700–740kt (vs 969.4kt) — sharp step-down
  • Nickel: 70–80kt (vs 71.9kt)
  • Steelmaking coal: 30–34mt (vs 32.5mt)
  • Energy coal: 95–100mt (vs 98.0mt)
  • Shares +2.0% to 564.10p in London; +1.8% to ZAR127.91 in Johannesburg on the day.

  • Weather losses spiked to $17.2m (7.8pts) vs $8.6m (3.7pts) — well above 5-year Q1 average of 4.5pts.
  • Large fire losses $12.2m (5.5pts) vs $7.7m (3.3pts), driven by higher frequency and severity (+$2.3m commercial property, +$2.2m homeowner).

  • Net investment income +19.2% to $14.3m on higher yields (avg yield 3.8% vs 3.6%) and higher invested assets.
  • Total investments $1.50bn; 95.3% in fixed maturities; duration 5.7 years.
  • Statutory commercial multi-peril combined ratio jumped to 113.9% vs 90.3%; workers' comp improved to 112.9% vs 117.6%; personal homeowners deteriorated to 94.6% vs 83.8%.
  • Quarterly dividends declared: $0.1925 Class A / $0.175 Class B, payable 15 May 2026.

• Gross premiums written (GPW) $668.4m, down $43.7m (-6.1%) YoY; excluding prior-year reinstatement premiums, underlying top-line decline was ~1.2%.
  • Group Renewal Price Index (RPI) 93% (reinsurance 92%, insurance 94%) — indicating continued rate pressure at renewals.
  • Segment GPW: Reinsurance $411.0m (down $71.3m / -14.8%); Insurance $257.4m (up $27.6m / +12.0%).
  • Insurance revenue $468.6m, up $9.7m / +2.1% YoY (reinsurance revenue -0.9%; insurance revenue +4.9%).
  • Loss environment “relatively benign”; exposure to Middle East conflict stated as limited and within risk appetite.
  • Total investment return 0.3% (incl unrealised gains/losses); portfolio duration 2.2 years (2.0 years prior), credit quality A+, book yield 4.6%; managed investments $3.22bn (vs $3.10bn).
  • Management actions: executed a planned reduction in inwards property retrocession in reinsurance; offset by insurance-line growth (notably energy and marine) and continued build-out of Lancashire US franchise.
  • Lloyd’s platform: after acquiring 100% underwriting capacity for Syndicate 2010 from 2026 YoA, intends (subject to Lloyd’s approval) to combine Syndicates 3010 and 2010 under Syndicate 3010 for 2027+ YoA.
  • Senior management transitions: Rachel Sabbarton and Jennifer Wilson succeeded John Spence and Hayley Johnston as CEOs of Lloyd’s and Bermuda platforms respectively.
  • CEO Alex Maloney (quote):“Lancashire has had a positive start to 2026, holding fast to our core principle of active cycle management.

With the strong first quarter, we are on track to deliver results in line with our guidance for the year.

As part of our proactive approach to managing the cycle, we enacted a planned reduction in inwards property retrocession in our reinsurance segment. This was offset by a 12% increase in gross premiums written across our insurance lines to $257.4 million, where we saw attractive opportunities for growth. Insurance revenue increased by just over 2% to $468.6 million, reflecting earnings from the growth delivered over the past few years.

As we move through 2026, we will continue to maximise opportunities where it makes sense, and we have the teams and talent across our Group to do this. The work we have done over recent years to grow our product portfolio and increase our geographic reach puts us in a strong position to continue to generate attractive risk-adjusted underwriting returns through the cycle.

Clearly, the period has seen very significant geopolitical volatility leading to wider economic uncertainty. Lancashire’s exposure to the current events in the Middle East is limited and well within our risk appetite.

The Group’s investment portfolio, including unrealised gains and losses, returned 0.3% over the period.

Since acquiring 100% of the underwriting capacity for Syndicate 2010, with effect from the 2026 year of account, we have been assessing the increased optionality that full alignment offers us. Subject to approval by Lloyd’s, we will combine Lancashire Syndicates 3010 and 2010, under Syndicate 3010, for the 2027 and subsequent years of account.

During the quarter, we also saw planned senior management transitions in our Lloyd’s and Bermuda platforms, with Rachel Sabbarton and Jennifer Wilson, respectively succeeding John Spence and Hayley Johnston as CEOs. Our thanks go to John and Hayley for their valued contributions to Lancashire’s success over many years.

For more than two decades, Lancashire has flexibly managed the (re)insurance cycle with a focus on disciplined risk selection, strong capital management, and adding value in our relationships with clients and brokers. We remain fully focused on keeping our momentum as we drive the business further forward, and we maintain our expectation of a stable top-line, and a high teens RoE for 2026.”

time_period: New Five-Year Plan to FY31 (vs FY26 baseline; includes FY27 transition impacts)
body:
• CEO Dominic Paul: "For over 280 years, Whitbread's success has been driven by continually evolving to meet the needs of our guests. Today our business is built around a world-class brand in Premier Inn, which is synonymous with great quality and value, and has an unrivalled market position in the UK as well as a hugely exciting opportunity in Germany.

"We always challenge ourselves to improve and, in light of significant cost increases in the form of business rates and National Insurance, as well as the implied market discount to our inherent value, we've looked hard at the options open to us to maximise value creation over the medium and long-term. This has been a rigorous process and we've approached all options with an open mind.

"Our conclusion is that our model is the right one... we will refocus our capital spend and recycle more of our freehold real estate, driving increased margins and returns, reducing our capital intensity and increasing cash returns for shareholders...

"In the UK... convert all our remaining branded restaurants to an integrated food and beverage offer... unlock the addition of more highly profitable extension rooms...

"In Germany... now that we have reached profitability... focus on formats and locations which we know deliver the best return...

"This plan will transform Whitbread into a higher-margin, higher-returning pure-play hotel business..."

  • Plan headline outcomes by FY31 (vs FY26): £275m incremental adjusted PBT contribution, £1bn reduction in gross capex and >£1bn reduction in net capex, +500bps Group ROCE, and £2bn free cash flow available for shareholder returns.
  • Funding shift: growth capex to be funded through recycling £1.5bn of freehold real estate; move increasingly to leasehold growth; reduce freehold proportion from ~50% to 30–40% over time.
  • Net capex targeted at ~£200m–£250m per year, representing >£1bn reduction versus the previous five-year plan.
  • UK & Ireland growth plan: reallocate capital to highest-return opportunities while still growing open rooms to 96,000 by FY31 (retaining longer-term potential to reach up to 125,000 rooms thereafter).
  • Accelerating Growth Plan extended: replace all remaining 197 branded restaurants with integrated F&B; expected to enable more higher-return extension rooms and deliver 15%–20% returns on capital by FY31.
  • Restaurant disposals: agreed sale of 51 branded restaurants for £50m; agreed terms (subject to conditions) for sale of a further 60 sites.
  • FY27 transition impact: £40m reduction in adjusted PBT as remaining branded restaurants transition; after offsetting original AGP benefits, net £10m reduction to adjusted PBT in FY27 (subject to required employee consultation).
  • Cost & commercial programme: commercial initiatives to sustain UK outperformance; cost efficiencies target increased to £250m by FY31.
  • Germany: having reached profitability in FY26, growth focus shifts to accelerate FCF/ROIC; still targeting >50% room growth to 18,000 rooms by FY31 (with portfolio/pipeline optimisation proposed).
  • Shareholder returns: plan implies substantial FCF for dividends and buybacks, but share buy-backs paused in FY27 due to incremental AGP investment.

body:
• CEO Gary Nagle: "Building on our operational delivery over the past two years, first quarter production was largely in line with our expectations, accounting for operational conditions and the Lady Loretta (zinc) and Mount Isa copper mines in Australia reaching their planned economic end of lives during 2025. Accordingly, full year 2026 production guidance remains unchanged from that presented at our Capital Markets Day in December 2025.

"While the Middle East conflict has created numerous dislocations, particularly around the supply of crude, refined products and sulphuric acid, our energy marketing business has supported the supply of fuels to our assets. In addition, our significant metallurgical asset footprint, across copper, zinc and nickel, puts Glencore in a net-long global sulphuric acid position. Although the impact of the conflict on our industrial business was limited in the first quarter, recent and emerging impacts are now manifesting, primarily as an increase in input costs, most notably diesel and acid consumption, and the generally weaker USD.

"Critically, basis the current stronger commodity prices (e.g. year-to-date copper +c.5%, zinc +c.7% and energy coal +c.22%), we expect these cost impacts to be more than offset, which would result in margin expansion. In addition, extrapolating our Q1 Marketing performance, would see this segment's full-year EBIT performance comfortably exceeding the top end of our long-term Adjusted EBIT guidance range of $2.3-3.5bn p.a."

  • FY26 production guidance unchanged vs Capital Markets Day (Dec 2025): Copper 810–870kt, Zinc 700–740kt, Nickel 70–80kt, Steelmaking coal 30–34mt, Energy coal 95–100mt.
  • Own-sourced production (Q1 2026 vs Q1 2025): Copper 199.6kt (+19%); Cobalt 5.8kt (-39%); Zinc 176.9kt (-17%); Lead 41.2kt (-17%); Nickel 17.2kt (-9%); Gold 68koz (-53%); Silver 4,869koz (+15%); Chrome ore 830kt (+3%); Steelmaking coal 6.5mt (-22%); Energy coal 22.9mt (-2%).
  • Copper +31.7kt YoY driven by improved grades at African copper (+27.4kt) and higher throughput/grades at Antamina (+13.5kt); partly offset by Mount Isa copper mine closure impact (-8.9kt).
  • Cobalt -3.7kt YoY due to DRC export quota system introduced late 2025: DRC assets prioritising copper as existing cobalt inventories sufficient for near-term quotas.
  • Zinc -36.7kt YoY mainly from Lady Loretta end of mine life (-22.3kt) and lower Kazzinc contribution (-13.8kt) due to own-sourced feedstock sequencing.
  • Nickel -1.6kt YoY due to 2025 Sudbury furnace disruption impacting matte shipment lead times to Norway.
  • Steelmaking coal -1.8mt YoY due to pit sequencing at EVR, wet weather (Queensland) and planned longwall move at Oaky Creek.
  • H2-weighted guidance drivers: Collahuasi (ore + desalinated water improving), steelmaking coal (Canada pit sequencing + Oaky Creek longwall move), energy coal (Ulan longwall move in H1; lower strip ratios at Bulga/Cerrejón in H2).
  • DRC cobalt update: quota system applies until at least end-2027; excess production stored in-country and sold “as circumstances allow”; may hold cobalt in solution/not reported as production to minimise processing costs.
  • DRC govt extended validity of 2025 quotas to April 2026; Glencore exported most of its 2025 quota in Q1, remainder exported in April 2026; unused Q1 2026 quotas valid until 30 June 2026.
  • Expected cobalt export quota allocation (kt): 2026 (incl. 2025 carryover) 22.8kt (KCC 16.1; Mutanda 6.7) vs 2027 18.8kt (KCC 13.3; Mutanda 5.5).

body:
• At AGM, Chair Stuart Chambers described 2025 as “highly consequential” in the context of merger/disposal plans.
  • Merger plan: combine with Teck Resources to form “Anglo Teck”, positioned as “one of the world’s largest copper producers”; completion targeted later in 2026 or early 2027.
  • Governance: new board to be announced; Sheila Murray named as chair of Anglo Teck; Anglo and Teck each to nominate 50% of the non-executive board.
  • Chambers: “Despite the volatility in the world around us, we made great strides in 2025 to ensure that Anglo American is a more agile and resilient business...”
  • Strategic focus reiterated: copper, premium iron ore, and crop nutrients, aligned to “structural trends of decarbonisation, improving living standards, and food security”.
  • Portfolio progress cited: sale of Anglo American Platinum (now Valterra Platinum).
  • Disposals still in progress: steelmaking coal, nickel, and De Beers diamond operations.
  • CEO Duncan Wanblad on failed Peabody coal deal: “While we were very disappointed that Peabody decided not to complete... we expect that we will successfully reach an alternative sales agreement for value in 2026.”
  • Safety: Wanblad called the deaths of two employees in Brazil and Zimbabwe last year “simply unacceptable” and reiterated safety priority.
  • Chambers: “In a year characterised by volatile markets and slow economic recovery in China, and with weaker iron ore prices and cyclically low diamond prices, Anglo American delivered a stable operating and financial performance.”

  • Financial: SDO net revenue $78.7m, up 44% QoQ (Q2: $54.8m).

  • Dividend: interim dividend for FY2026 2.00p per share declared Feb 2026 and paid in April 2026 (post period-end).
  • Safety: operations were LTI-free during the quarter; milestones included Doornbosch five years total injury free; Lannex/Lesedi/Millsell five/six/four years LTI-free (as stated in the release).
  • Guidance: expects to achieve or exceed upper end of previously increased PGM production guidance (90,000–93,000 4E oz).
  • Guidance change: chrome concentrate production guidance revised to 50,000–55,000 tons (ROM feed quality and weather-related challenges in recent weeks).
  • CEO Jaco Prinsloo: “I am pleased to report the Company had another strong Quarter, especially at the SDO, with the production of 22,853 4E PGM ounces, which, due to the usual Christmas break, was a slight decrease from the record production achieved in Q2 and Q1 FY2026, but in line with expectations for the Period. Consequently, the Company is likely to achieve or exceed the upper end of the previously increased PGM production guidance of 90,000 to 93,000 4E PGM ounces, announced in the last quarter.

After successfully transitioning into production, the Thaba JV continues to build operational momentum, and the plant throughput and Chrome production for the past quarter were in line with the revised ramp-up plan communicated in February 2026. However, post Period-end, lower ROM feed tonnage and feed grade negatively impacted overall plant performance, while abnormally high rainfall during April 2026 has further impacted mining production volumes and plant throughput due to flooding and material handling challenges with the wet ore. As a result, chrome production guidance for FY2026 has been revised to between 50,000 and 55,000 tons. The focus remains on improving mine planning, scheduling optimisation, and mining standards to improve ROM feed quality, plant feed stability and throughput, and enhancing processing efficiencies as we progress towards steady-state operations.

In April, a tragic incident occurred at the Tweefontein Operation, whereby a Phoenix Security Officer, a contractor for the Company, lost his life during a criminal attack while on duty. The Board of Sylvania sends its heartfelt condolences to the individual's family, friends and colleagues.

We are committed to the safety and security of our employees and contractors and, during the Quarter, recorded zero LTIs across the SDO and Thaba JV Operations. We also achieved several key safety milestones, including Doornbosch reaching five years Total Injury free, Lannex six years LTI-free, Lesedi three years LTI-free and Millsell one-year Total Injury free and four years LTI-free.

From a financial perspective, the average 4E gross basket price increased by 28% in USD and 23% in Rand ("ZAR") terms, and this, together with the increased contribution from attributable Chrome sales of $4.0 million, resulted in an improved net revenue performance of $78.7 million (Q2 FY2026: $54.8 million).

The adjusted Group EBITDA for the Quarter rose to $47.8 million (Q2 FY2026: $29.8 million), which is a significant 61% increase quarter-on-quarter, and similarly to revenue, increased as a result of the increased gross 4E basket price and Chrome sales contribution.”

We have also identified further opportunities in digitisation, plant network optimisation and SG&A efficiency, which are expected to support continued improvement and provide momentum over the next 18-24 months.

Our upgraded 4PRO full solutions value propositions to selected customers show encouraging feedback from leading, sophisticated customers in their markets.

time_period: Ongoing (Middle East war-driven fuel shock; schedule actions cited for May–October and through October)
body:
• Closure of the Strait of Hormuz described as materially tightening oil supply and pushing jet fuel prices sharply higher, prompting airlines to cut capacity.
  • Consumer-facing commentary (Travel Therapy TV host Karen Schaler) quote: "Travel alert: airlines are cutting thousands of flights right now... Book early."
  • Analyst comment (Goodbody’s Dudley Shanley): "It is not unusual for carriers to adjust their schedules at this time of the year," but if jet fuel stays elevated, "there will have to be a little bit more trimming for low-cost airlines".
  • EU Energy Commissioner Dan Jorgensen (Sky News) quote: "Unfortunately, it's very likely that many people's holidays will be affected, either by flight cancellations or very, very expensive tickets."
  • Air Transat cut 6% of its May–October schedule.
  • AirAsia X: earlier said fares up to 40% and about 10% of flights cut so far; further cuts announced without a total figure.
  • Lufthansa: announced 20,000 flights cut through October, and halting regional feeder CityLine (per excerpt).
  • Air France-KLM: trimmed 2% of flights in May and June at Transavia; KLM cancellations held to ~1% of European flights.
  • Ryanair: did not cite fuel directly in Berlin cuts (from October), pointing to high costs/taxes; also cutting 10% of flights from Dublin (airport capacity criticism).
  • Volotea: trimmed ~1% of flights from its summer schedule since the beginning of the month.
  • Wizz Air: CEO Jozsef Varadi quote on not cutting capacity: "We are not taking capacity out, because I think the other guys will take capacity out... You don't have to run faster than the bear, but faster than the guy next to you."

body:
